In al-Mukhtār: «The ḥaẓīra is made for camels from trees to protect them from cold and wind, and the muḥtaẓir, with kasra on the ẓāʾ, is the one who makes it». The meaning is that they became like dry, crumbled trees when shattered; الهشيم is what is broken up and crumbled.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ) A past verb and an agent; بالنذر: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to كذبت. It has been said before that النذر is either a maṣdar, with the meaning of warning (al-indhār), or the plural of نذير, i.e. a warner. (فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا واحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قالوا a past verb and an agent. In أبشرا the hamza is interrogative, and بشرا is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation), i.e. by an implied verb explained by what follows: "shall we follow a mortal?". منا is an adjective of بشرا; واحدا has two possible analyses, the clearer being that it is an adjective of بشرا, except that this is problematic as the interpreted adjective is fronted before the explicit adjective; the reply is that منا is then not an adjective but a ḥāl from واحدا, fronted before it. The second analysis is that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in نتبعه; and بشر applies to the singular and the plural. نتبعه: an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; إن with its noun; إذن is a particle of answer and recompense, inoperative; لفي: the lām is the shifted lām, and في ضلال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element which is the khabar of إن; and سعر is conjoined to ضلال. (أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ) The hamza is for a question of denial; ألقي is a passive past verb and الذكر a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʾil); عليه: attached to ألقي; من بيننا is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in عليه, i.e. singled out; بل is a particle of rejoinder and conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ, كذاب its khabar and أشر an adjective. (سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ) The clauses are the content of an omitted saying, its implied form being "Allah the Exalted said"; the sīn is for the future; يعلمون a verb and an agent; غدا an adverb attached to يعلمون; من an interrogative noun, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and الكذاب its khabar and الأشر an adjective; the clause is suspended (muʿallaqa) because the interrogative stands at its head, and it fills the place of the two objects of يعلمون. (إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ وَاصْطَبِرْ) إن with its noun, and مرسلو الناقة is its khabar; the clause is resumptive, to explain what was promised; فتنة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. as a test for them; the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; ارتقبهم: an imperative, a latent agent and a direct object; واصطبر is conjoined to ارتقبهم, and what اصطبر is attached to is omitted, i.e. "and be patient with their harm". (وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْماءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; نبئهم: an imperative verb, a latent agent, the implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is the first object; أن and what is in its scope are in the position of the second and third objects, because نبّأ takes three objects; أن with its noun, and قسمة is its khabar; بينهم is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of قسمة (mentioned as "divided"), or to قسمة because it means "divided"; كل is a mubtadaʾ, شرب a muḍāf ilayhi, and محتضر the khabar of كل, i.e. attended by them or by the she-camel. (فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; نادوا a past verb and an agent; what it is conjoined upon is omitted, i.e. "they persisted in that"; and it is better to take it as the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. they remained so for a time, then grew weary of the drying up of the water and the barrenness of the pastures, and agreed to kill her and concurred on lying in wait for her where she passed, and Qudār ibn Sālif volunteered for this matter, whose story has been given before; so they called him and he took it up. صاحبهم is a direct object; فتعاطى is conjoined to فنادوا, i.e. he dared to take up this matter without regard for it; فعقر is conjoined to تعاطى. (فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ) its i'rab was given shortly before. (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ) إن with its noun, and the clause أرسلنا is its khabar; عليهم: attached to أرسلنا; صيحة is a direct object and واحدة an adjective; فكانوا is conjoined to أرسلنا, the wāw being the noun of كان, and الهشيم المحتظر its khabar [Translator's note: the source writes «الهشيم المحتظر»; the verse has كهشيم المحتظر]. It was also read with fatḥa (المحتظَر), as a noun of place, which is the place of enclosure-making, i.e. the ḥaẓīra. (وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ) its i'rab was given shortly before.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «سيعلمون غدا من الكذاب الأشر» there is the art of vagueness (fann al-ibhām), so that the threat is more charged with vengeance and the menace more potent in souls. He gave it in the form of vagueness although they were the ones meant, because He intended the time of death and did not intend a specific tomorrow; this is common in Arabic poetry. Abū al-Ṭammāḥ said:
ألا عللاني قبل نوح النوائح ... وقبل اضطراب النفس بين الجوانح
وقبل غد يا لهف نفسي في غد ... إذا راح أصحابي ولست برائح
(Distract me before the wailing of the mourning women, and before the soul convulses between the ribs; and before tomorrow, alas for my soul on that tomorrow, when my companions depart and I do not depart.)
He meant the time of death and did not intend a specific tomorrow. Of this too is the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
للموت فيها سهام غير مخطئة ... من لم يكن ميتا في اليوم مات غدا
(Death has arrows in it that do not miss; whoever does not die today dies tomorrow.)
2- Simile: In His saying «فكانوا كهشيم المحتظر» there is a loose simile (tashbīh mursal) for their destruction and annihilation.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ﴾. It has been mentioned that it split, and that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd saw (Mount) Ḥirāʾ between its two halves, the two halves of the moon.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَرَوْاْ آيَةً...﴾ — He means the moon — ﴿يُعْرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحْرٌ مُّسْتَمِرٌّ﴾.
That is: it will come to nothing and pass away.
Some of them said: magic, part of which resembles another.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ﴾.
The outcome of their denial will settle, and the outcome of the saying of those who believe, until they know its reality through punishment and reward.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ بَالِغَةٌ﴾.
It is nominative as conjoined to (ما فيه مُزْدجَر), and (ما) is in the position of a nominative. Had you made it nominative as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), as though you were explaining (ما) by it, it would have been correct; and had it been accusative by «qaṭʿ» (detachment, i.e. as ḥāl), since it is indefinite while «ما» is definite, it would have been correct.
Similar to it in its being nominative is: ﴿هذا ما لدىَّ عتيدٌ﴾; had (عتيدٌ) been accusative, it would have been correct. And His saying: ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ ٱلنُّذُرُ﴾.
If you wish, you make (ما) a negation, meaning: the warnings do not avail them; and if you wish, you put it in the position of «أىّ», as though you said: what then do the warnings avail? [187/ا]

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿خُشَّعاً أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾.
When the verb (here, the participle) comes before a feminine noun to which it belongs, or before a feminine plural such as «الأبصار», «الأعمار» and the like, it is permissible to make the verb feminine, masculine, or plural. All of that has come in this word: Ibn ʿAbbās read it (خاشعاً).
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told me:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym and Abū Muʿāwiya told me, from Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd, from Muslim ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read it (خاشعاً).
[Muḥammad told me:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym told me, from ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī, from al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, that one of them said (خاشعاً) and the other (خُشَّعاً).
Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (خاشِعةً أبصارُهُم), and the reading of the people since is (خُشعاً أبصارُهم).
The poet said:
وشبَابٍ حَسنٍ أوجُهُهُمْ * من إياد بن نزار نب مَعَدِّ
(And many a youth whose faces are fair, of Iyād son of Nizār son of Maʿadd.)
And another said:
يرمى الفِجاجَ الركبانُ مُعترضاً * أعناقَ بُزَّلِهَا مُرْخًى لها الجدُلُ
(The riders cast at the mountain passes, the necks of their full-grown camels stretched across, their reins slackened for them.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: «الجدُل» is the plural of «الجَديل», which is the halter. Had he said «مُعترضاتٍ» or «مُعترضةً» it would have been correct, and (likewise) «مُرْخاةً» and «مرخياتٍ».
«[Translator's note: «نب» in the verse is as printed, evidently for «بن».]»

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿مُّهْطِعِينَ﴾: looking towards the caller.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ﴾.
He was rebuked with insults. «ازْدُجِر» is the iftaʿala form from «زَجَرْتُ». When a word begins with zāy, the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form becomes dāl in it; of this are «زُجِرَ», «ازْدُجِرَ» and «مُزْدَجَرٌ», and of this also «المُزْدَلِف» and «يزداد», which are from the verb (pattern) «يَفتعِل»; so make analogy on this for whatever occurs.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿فَالْتَقَى ٱلمَآءُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾.
He meant the two waters: the water of the earth and the water of the sky. «التقاء» (meeting) is only possible for two nouns or more; it was only permissible with «الماء» because «الماء» can be plural and singular.
And His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾: decreed in the Mother of the Book.
It is said: it had been determined that the amount of the two waters was one. And it is said: it had been decreed for what Allah intended of punishing them.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحَمَلْنَاهُ﴾.
We carried Noah on (a thing) of planks, meaning the ship; ﴿وَدُسُرٍ﴾: the nails of the ship and its cords by which it is bound.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ﴾.
That is: (one who) was denied.
He is saying: We did to him and to them what We did as a recompense for what was done to Noah and his companions. He said «لِمَنْ» meaning the people, and it has the sense of «ما». Do you not see that you say: «غُرّقوا لنوحٍ» (they were drowned for Noah) and «لِما صُنعَ بنُوح» (for what was done to Noah), and the meaning is one?

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ تَّرَكْنَاهَا آيَةً﴾.
He is saying: We preserved it after Noah as a sign.
And His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ﴾.
The meaning is «مُذتَكرٍ». When you form «مُفْتعل» from a word whose first letter is dhāl, the dhāl and the tāʾ of iftiʿāl become a doubled dāl. Some of Banū Asad say «مُذّكرٌ»: they let the dhāl prevail, so it becomes a doubled dhāl.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Kisāʾī told me — [and by Allah, I have known him to be nothing but truthful] — from Isrāʾīl and al-Qarzamī, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, who said: We said to ʿAbd Allāh: «فهلم من مُذَّكرٍ» or «مُدَّكرٍ»? He said: The Messenger of Allah [187/ب] ﷺ taught me to recite: (مُدَّكِرٌ) with dāl.
«[Translator's note: «فهلم» is as printed, evidently for «فهل».]»

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾.
«النذر» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun), its meaning being: how then was My warning? Similar to it is ﴿عذراً أو نذراً﴾ (15); both are pronounced light (with sukūn) and heavy (with ḍamma), as He said ﴿إلى شَىء نُّكُرٍ﴾, which is heavy in "اقتربت" (al-Qamar) and light in the shorter Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, where it was said "نُكْراً".
«[Translator's note: «(15)» is as in the source; ﴿عذراً أو نذراً﴾ is Q 77:6.]»

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ﴾.
He is saying: We made it easy; were it not for that, the servants would not have been able to utter the speech of Allah. And it is said: «ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر» means for memorising; for there is no book that is memorised by heart other than it.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ﴾: it continued upon them with its ill-omen.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ﴾: their lower parts. «منقعر» means the felled palm tree.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ إِذاً لَّفِي ضَلاَلٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾. By «السُّعُر» He meant hardship, (as) of punishment.

farraa:25-26.t:
His saying: ﴿كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ﴾: Mujāhid alone read «الأَشُر».
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told me, from a man, from Mujāhid, that he read (سَيَعْلَمُونَ) with yāʾ — so Sufyān said — ﴿مَّنِ ٱلْكَذَّابُ ٱلأَشِرُ﴾. It is like your saying in speech: «رجل حَذِر» and «حَذُرٌ» (wary), «فطِنٌ» and «فطُنٌ» (astute), «عجِل» and «عَجُلٌ» (hasty).
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he read «سيعلمون غدا» with yāʾ.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾.
The she-camel has a day and they have a day; so He said «بينهم», (meaning) between them and the she-camel.
And His saying: ﴿كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُّحْتَضَرٌ﴾: its owners and whoever is entitled to it attend it.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾.
(The one) who fences in over his dry stubble. Al-Ḥasan alone read «كهشيم المحتظَر», with a fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, thus making «الهشيم» the muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) to «المحتظَر»; it is as He said: ﴿إِنَّ هذا لهو حقُّ اليقين﴾, where «الحق» is «اليقين»; and as He said: ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرةِ خَيْرٌ﴾, putting «الدار» in construct with «الآخرة», while it is the Hereafter itself. «الهشيم» is trees (and plants) when they dry up.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿نَّجَّيْنَاهُم بِسَحَرٍ﴾.
«سحر» here is fully declined (with nunation), because it is indefinite, as in your saying «نجيناهم بليلٍ» (We saved them by night). But when the Arabs drop the bāʾ from it, they do not decline it, and say: «فعلت هذا سحرَ يا هذا» (I did this at daybreak, you there). It is as though, in their not declining it, their speech had it with the article al-, and it ran on that basis; so when the alif and lām were dropped while they were still intended, it was not declined. The speech of the Arabs is to say «ما زال عندنا مذ السحر» (he has been with us since daybreak); they hardly say anything else.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَمَارَوْاْ بِٱلنُّذُرِ﴾: they denied what he told them.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُم بُكْرَةً عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: The Arabs decline «غدوة» and «بكرة» fully and also leave them undeclined; most usage with «غدوة» is to leave it undeclined, and most usage with «بكرة» is that it is declined.
He said: I heard one of them say: «أتيته بكرةَ باكرا» (I came to him early in the morning). Whoever does not decline it makes it definite, because it is a noun that always refers to one (fixed) time, like «أمس» (yesterday) and «غد» (tomorrow). The Arabs most often decline «غدوة» when it is paired with «عشية», saying: «إنى لآتيك غُدوةً وعشيةً» (I shall come to you morning and evening), and some of them say «غدوةً وعشيةَ»; and some of them do not decline «عشية» [188/ا] because of how often it has accompanied «غدوة».
«[Translator's note: «تجريمها» in the source is evidently a misprint for «تجريهما» (decline them).]»
And His saying: ﴿عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ﴾.
He is saying: a punishment that is real.

farraa:43-45.t:
His saying: ﴿أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أُوْلَئِكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: are your disbelievers, O people of Mecca, better than these whom the punishment struck, or do you have an immunity in the Scriptures? He is saying: or do you have an immunity from the punishment? Then He said: «أم يقولون», that is: «أيقولون» (do they say): we are a great host, victorious? So Allah said: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾, and that was the day of Badr.
He said «الدبر» in the singular and did not say «الأدبار»; all of it is permissible. It is correct to say «ضربْنا منهم الرءوس والأعين» (we struck their heads and eyes) and «ضربنا منهم الرأس واليد» (we struck their head and hand); and it is as you say «إنه لكثير الدينار والدرهم» (he has much dinar and dirham), meaning dinars and dirhams.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ﴾. He is saying: more grievous for them than the punishment of the day of Badr; and «أمرّ» is from «المرارة» (bitterness).

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "يوم يسحبون إلى النار على وجوههم".
And His saying: ﴿ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾. «سقر» is one of the names of Hell; it is not declined (a diptote). Every name of a feminine, whether it has the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) or does not have the hāʾ, is declined, except particular names that are light, and so were declined, while some left them undeclined; these are «هند», «دعد», «جُمل» and «رئم»: they are declined and not declined. Whoever does not decline them says: every feminine's due is not to be declined, because it has the sense of the hāʾ, even if it does not appear; do you not see that when you form its diminutive you say «هنيدة» and «دعيدة»? Whoever declines them says: they became light because of the quiescence of their middle letter, and the hāʾ was dropped and did not appear, so they became light and were declined.
«[Translator's note: «فهو يجرى» (is declined) is as printed; the argument requires «فهو لا يجرى» (is not declined).]»

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾, that is: a single time. This is about the Hour: like the twinkling of a flash.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ﴾. He means: every sin, small or great, is written down.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ﴾: its meaning is «أنهار» (rivers), and in its manner it is like His saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُولُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ (45). Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard the Arabs say: «أتينا فلاناً فكنّا في لحمةٍ ونبيذة» (we came to so-and-so and were amid meat and date-wine), using the singular while the meaning is plenty.
And it is said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ﴾ means in light and spaciousness. I heard one of the Arabs recite:
إِن تك ليليا فإنى نَهِرُ * متى أرى الصبح فلا أنتظرُ
(If you are a man of the night, I am a man of the day; when I see the morning I do not wait.)
The meaning of «نَهِر» is: a person of the day (nahār). It has been transmitted: "وما أمْرُنا إلاَّ وَحدةً" in the accusative; it is as though he implied a verb by which «الواحدة» is made accusative, as you say to a man: «ما أنت إلا ثيابَك مرة، ودابتك مرة، ورأسك مرة» (you are nothing but your clothes one time, your mount another, and your head another), that is: you attend to that.
Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: «إنما العامرى عِمَّتَه» (the ʿĀmirī is nothing but his turban), that is: he attends to nothing of his clothing but the turban. Al-Farrāʾ said: and I do not like the accusative of it in recitation.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «وإن يروا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «انشق القمر»; «سحر» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it".

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «كذَّبوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {يُعْرِضُوا}, and the clause «وكل أمر مستقر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent); the preposition «من الأنباء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما»; and the clause «فيه مزدجر» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «حكمة» is a badal (substitute) from {مَا}. The fāʾ is conjunctive; «ما» is negative; «تُغْن» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, which is omitted in writing following the pronunciation in connected speech, where it is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The clause «فما تغن النذر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {جَاءَهُمْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «فتولَّ» is resumptive; «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied "remember". «يَدْع» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw, which is omitted in writing; «الداع» is the fāʿil (agent), nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, which is omitted in writing; the preposition «إلى شيء» is attached to «يدع».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «خُشَّعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يخرجون»; placing the ḥāl before a fully conjugable verb is permissible. «أبصارهم» is the fāʿil of «خشعا». [In such cases] the broken plural is more common than the singular; as for the sound plural, as in «مررت بقوم كريمين آباؤهم» (I passed by people whose fathers are noble), it is interpreted according to the dialect of (أكلوني البراغيث) ("the fleas ate me"). The clause «يخرجون» is resumptive, and the clause «كأنهم جراد» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يخرجون».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «مهطعين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يَخْرُجُونَ}; «إلى الداع» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مُهْطعين»; the clause «يقول» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «كذبت» is resumptive, and the clause «فكذَّبوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كذَّبت». His words «مجنون»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he is mad", and the clause «وازدجر» is conjoined to the clause (هو مجنون).

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فدعا» is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition bāʾ; and the clause «فانتصر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ففتحنا» is resumptive; the preposition «بماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أبواب السماء», i.e. "(We opened them) accompanied by this water".

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «عيونا» is a tamyīz (specification); the clause «فالتقى الماء» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «فجَّرنا»; and the clause «قد قُدِر» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أمر».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «وحملناه» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «التقى الماء».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «تجري» is a naʿt (adjective) of {ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ}; the preposition «بأعيننا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تجري»; «جزاء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «لمن» is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) «جزاء».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The wāw is resumptive; «آية» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ. «مدَّكر» is mubtadaʾ (subject), «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "so is there anyone who will take heed?" The original form of «مُدَّكِر» is مُذْتَكِر: the dhāl was changed to dāl, then the tāʾ was changed to dāl, then the dāl was assimilated into the dāl.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar (predicate) of «كان»; «نُذُر» is a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «عذابي», nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The wāw is resumptive; «مُدَّكر» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The fāʾ in «فكيف» is resumptive; see the i'rab of verse (16).

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The preposition «في يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «تنزع» is a naʿt (adjective) of {رِيحًا}; the clause «كأنهم أعجاز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الناس».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «فقالوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {كَذَّبَتْ}. «بشرا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it; the preposition «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بشرا», and «واحدا» is a naʿt; the clause «نتبعه» is explicative. The clause «إنا لفي ضلال» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and «إذًا» is a particle of response.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «أؤلقي» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the preposition «من بيننا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليه».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «سيعلمون» is resumptive; «من» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الكذَّاب» is the khabar (predicate); the clause «مَن الكذَّاب» stands in place of the two objects of «علم», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «فتنة» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فتنة»; and the clause «فارتقبهم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «إنَّا مرسلو».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «ونبئهم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «اصطبر»; «أنَّ» and what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), stands in place of the second and third objects. «بينهم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «قسمة». The clause «كل شرب محتضر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «فنادوا» is resumptive, and the clause «فتعاطى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «نادوا».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and «كيف» is an interrogative noun, the khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «فكانوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أرسلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «مُدَّكر» is mubtadaʾ (subject), «من» is redundant (zāʾida), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "there". The clause «فهل من مُدَّكر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يَسَّرْنا».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «آل» is excepted, accusative (manṣūb); the clause «نجَّيناهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «نعمة» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the preposition «مِنْ عندنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نعمة». The clause «نجزي» is resumptive, and the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "We recompense him with a recompense like that recompense".

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The wāw is resumptive, and the clause «فتماروا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أنذرهم».

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: (ولقد راودوه عن ضيفه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أنذرهم»; the clause «فطمسنا» is conjoined to the clause «راودوه», and the clause «فذوقوا» is conjoined to the clause «طمسنا».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «بكرة» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; it is declined as a triptote because it is indefinite; had a specific time been intended by it, it would have been a diptote because of definiteness and the feminine.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «فذوقوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {صَبَّحَهُمْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The wāw in «ولقد» is resumptive; «مُدَّكر» is mubtadaʾ (subject) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «فهل من مدَّكر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يسَّرنا».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: (ولقد جاء آل فرعون النذر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw in «ولقد» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «كذَّبوا» is resumptive; the clause «فأخذناهم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «كذَّبوا»; «أَخْذَ» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «أكفاركم خير» is resumptive; the preposition «من أولئكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير». The clause «لكم براءة» is resumptive, and «أم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa); the preposition «في الزبر» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «براءة».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «يقولون» is resumptive; «جميع» is the khabar (predicate), and «منتصر» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جميع».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: (سيهزم الجمع ويولون الدبر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted (تقول), i.e. "the keepers will say on the day"; the clause «ذوقوا» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of the implied saying. The preposition «على وجوههم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, and «سقر» is a diptote because it is a proper name and feminine in meaning.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: «كلَّ» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «خلقناه» is explicative; the preposition «بقدر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «خلقناه»; and the implied clause (خلقنا) is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «وما أمرنا إلا واحدة» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ}; the preposition «كلمح» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «واحدة»; the preposition «بالبصر» is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) (لمح).

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The wāw is resumptive, and the clause «فهل من مدَّكر» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أهلكنا».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The preposition «في الزبر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «كل»; the clause (وكل شيء في الزبر) is resumptive, and the clause «فعلوه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كل شيء».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: (وكل صغير وكبير مستطر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding resumptive clause; «مستطر» is the khabar (predicate) of «كل».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The preposition «في مقعد» is a badal (substitute) from {فِي جَنَّاتٍ}; the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, مزدجر: the دال is a substitute for a تاء, and it is the pattern مُفتعَل from الزجر (restraining). The دال was substituted for the تاء only because the تاء is voiceless (mahmūs) and the زاي is voiced (majhūr), and their points of articulation are close to each other; so they substituted for the تاء a letter from its point of articulation that agrees with the زاي in voicing, namely the دال.
His saying مدكر: its origin is مذتكر, so it is the pattern مُفتعِل from الذكر (remembering). But the ذال is a voiced, strong letter and the تاء is voiceless and weak, so they substituted for the تاء a letter from its point of articulation that agrees with the ذال in voicing, namely the دال; then the ذال was assimilated into the دال. مُذَّكِر with the ذال is also permissible, by assimilating the second into the first, and Qatāda read thus.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying حِكْمَة: nominative as a badal (substitute) of ما in His saying ما فيه مزدجر — and ما is nominative by جاء, as its fāʿil (agent) — or by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is wisdom" (هي حكمة).
His saying فَمَا تغن النّذر: ما is interrogative and may be in the position of the accusative by تغني; it may also be negating, with the object of تغني omitted.
The yāʾ was omitted from تغني, and the wāw from يدع الداع, and the like, in the script of the Muṣḥaf, because it was written according to the pronunciation in continuous, connected speech, and was not written according to the rule of the origin and of the pause. Some grammarians erred and said: the yāʾ was omitted in فما تغن النذر only because ما is equivalent to لم, so it put the verb in the jussive as لم does. This is a mistake, because لم only negates and turns the future into the past, whereas ما negates the present; so neither may stand in the place of the other, because their meanings differ.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying يَوْم يدع: يوم is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "remember the day the caller calls" (اذكر يوم يدع). تولّ does not govern it, because the turning away is in this world and the day the caller calls is in the Hereafter; for that reason it is good to pause on عنهم and begin with يوم يدع الداع. It is also possible that the governing word in يوم is خشعا or يخرجون.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying خشعا: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the هاء and the ميم in عنهم, so pausing on عنهم is ugly; if you make it a ḥāl of the pronoun in يخرجون, pausing on عنهم is good. Likewise the position of يخرجون is a ḥāl of the genitive pronoun in أبصارهم; likewise the position of كأنهم جراد is a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in يخرجون; and likewise the position of مهطعين. All of them are accusative as ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying فَالتقى المَاء: الماء is a generic noun (ism jins); therefore He did not say الماءان, after mentioning the water's coming out from two places, from the sky and the earth. The origin of ماء is موه; they substituted an alif for the wāw because it was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa, so it became ماه. The alif is faint (khafiyya) and the هاء is faint, so two faint letters, the second and third radicals (ʿayn and lām), came together; so they substituted for the هاء a strong, firm letter, namely the hamza. What indicates this assumed origin is their saying in the plural أمواه and مياه, and in the diminutive مُوَيْه, so it was returned to its origin. [Translator's note: the edition prints «فَصَارَت مَاء» ("so it became ماء") at the intermediate stage, where the argument requires ماه; and «موية» for the diminutive مويه.]

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying وَلَقَد تركناها: the هاء refers to the punishment; it is also said: to the ship.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying فَكيف كَانَ عَذَابي وَنذر: كيف is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and عذابي its noun. It is also possible that كيف is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and كان means "occurred, happened" (complete كان), with العذاب nominative by كان, and it has no khabar.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying ريحًا صَرْصَرًا: its origin is صرَّر, from the thing [i.e. صرّ الشيء] when it makes a sound; but they substituted a صاد for the second رآء.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying تنْزع النَّاس كَأَنَّهُمْ أعجاز نخل منقعر: تنزع is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ريح, and كأنهم is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الناس; its implied form is "We sent upon them a furious wind, tearing out the people, they resembling the trunks of palm trees" — and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. they will be like that. It has also been said that the كاف is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "so it leaves them like the trunks of palm trees" (فتتركهم كأعجاز نخل), i.e. like the trunks of palm trees.
His saying نخل منقعر: منقعر was only made masculine because نخل is treated as masculine and feminine; therefore He said منقعر, and in another place He said أعجاز نخل خاوية, making it feminine.
His saying وَنذر: it is said to be a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "My warning" (إنذاري); it is also said to be the plural of نذير.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying أبشرا منا وَاحِد: accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "Shall we follow a single human being from among us?" (أنتبع بشرا منا واحدا); His saying نتبعه indicates the omission. منا and واحدا are two adjectives of بشر.
His saying وسعر: it is said to be the maṣdar of سَعِرَ الرجل, when he is frantic; it is also said to be the plural of سعير.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying من الْكذَّاب: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative by سيعلمون.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying فتنه لَهُم: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it is also said: a maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying واصطبر: it is افتعل from الصبر (patience), and its origin is اصتبر; they substituted for the تاء a letter akin to the صاد in emphasis (iṭbāq), namely the طاء, so that the tongue would perform a single action in the emphasis. Like it is مصطبر, which is مُفتعِل from الصبر; the proof is that when you form the diminutive or the plural you omit the طاء, since it is a substitute for a تاء: you say مُصَيْبِر and مَصابِر, as you do with مكتسب.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t:
His saying إِلَّا آل لوط: آل is accusative as the excepted. Its origin is أهل; then they substituted a hamza for the هاء because of its faintness, so it became أأل; then they substituted an alif for the quiescent hamza, as they did in آتى and آمن. What indicates that is their saying in the diminutive أُهَيْل.
His saying بِسحر: it is fully declined only because it is indefinite; were it definite it would be a diptote, because when it is definite it is deflected (maʿdūl) from the alif and lām, since it becomes definite by something other than them, while the right of this kind is to become definite by them; so when it did not become definite by them, it became deflected from them, and it became heavy, along with the heaviness of definiteness, so it was a diptote. If it is made indefinite, it is fully declined. Like it is بكرة, except that بكرة [when definite] is a diptote because of femininity and definiteness; and like it is غدوة; if the two are made indefinite they are fully declined, like سحر.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying نعْمَة من عندنَا: نعمة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). In ordinary speech the nominative is permissible, on the assumption "that is a favour" (تلك نعمة).
His saying كَذَلِك نجزي: the كاف is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "We recompense whoever is grateful with a recompense like that" (نجزي من شكر جزاء كذلك), i.e. like that.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying عَن ضَيفه: the Arabs hardly ever put ضيف in the dual or the plural, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); the implied form of the verse is "from the people of his guest" (عن ذوي ضيفه). Some of them have put it in the dual and the plural.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t:
His saying إِنَّا كل شَيْء خلقناه بِقدر: the preferred choice according to the principles of the Basrans would have been to put كل in the nominative, just as the preferred choice according to them in your saying زيد ضربته ("Zayd, I struck him") is the nominative. The preferred choice according to the Kufans in it is the accusative — unlike our saying زيد أكرمته — because in the verse something has preceded that governs what follows it, namely إنّ; so the preferred choice according to them in it is the accusative. The readers have agreed on the accusative in كل, according to the preferred choice in it among the Kufans, so that it would indicate the generality of things, the created things, that they belong to Allah — contrary to what the people of deviation said, that there are created things belonging to other than Allah; Allah is exalted above that. And His saying, Exalted is He, الله خالق كل شيء refutes their claim.
The accusative in كل indicates generality only because the implied form is "We created everything; We created it in measure" (إنا خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر), so خلقناه is an emphasis and explanation of the implied خلقنا that makes كل accusative. If you omit it and make the first overt, the implied form becomes "We created everything in measure" (إنا خلقنا كل شيء بقدر); this is a general expression that encompasses all created things. It is not permissible for خلقناه to be an adjective of شيء, because the adjective and the ṣila (relative clause) do not govern what comes before the thing described or the relative, nor do they explain what governs what comes before them. Since خلقناه is not an adjective of شيء, nothing remains but that it is an emphasis and explanation of the implied [verb] that makes كل accusative, and that indicates generality.
Also, the accusative is the preferred choice according to the Kufans because إنّ, according to them, seeks the verb and so is more suited to it; so the accusative in كل is the preferred choice according to them. When the sense of generality and of escaping ambiguity is added to that, the accusative is much stronger than the nominative.
Abū Muḥammad [i.e. Makkī] said: I have devoted a separate treatment to this question, more exhaustive than this explanation, in a book other than this one.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر﴾: اقتربت الساعة is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and انشق القمر is conjoined to the preceding clause.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وإن يروا آية يعرضوا ويقولوا سحر مستمر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; إن is conditional; يروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); يعرضوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); يقولوا is conjoined to ﴿يعرضوا﴾; سحر is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هذا (this); and مستمر is a naʿt (adjective) of سحر.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وكذبوا واتبعوا أهواءهم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; كذبوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); اتبعوا is a verb and its fāʿil; and أهواءهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وكل أمر مستقر﴾: the wāw is for resumption; كل أمر is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and مستقر is its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. It has been said: كل is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e.: acted upon; or it is conjoined to الساعة.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿ولقد جاءهم من الأنباء ما فيه مزدجر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; the lām falls in the answer to an implied oath; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); جاءهم is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ومن الأنباء is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ما; ما is relative or an indefinite qualified noun (mawṣūfa), and on both views it is the fāʿil (agent) of جاءهم; وفيه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ومزدجر: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause ﴿فيه مزدجر﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿حكمة بالغة﴾: حكمة is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a badal (substitute) from ﴿ما﴾ in the previous ayah; بالغة is a naʿt (adjective) of حكمة; and the object of بالغة is omitted, the implied form being: reaching its goal.
﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ما is negating, i.e.: the warnings availed nothing. Or ﴿ما﴾ is interrogative, for disapproval, in the position of the accusative as a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied form being: so what availing do the warnings avail?; or in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied form being: so what thing do the warnings avail?
﴿تغن﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, which was dropped in connected speech because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
﴿النذر﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of تغن.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿فتول عنهم يوم يدع الداع إلى شيء نكر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); تول is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: أنت (you); وعنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تول﴾; يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿يخرجون﴾, or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being: اذكر (remember); the clause يدع is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الداعي is the fāʿil of يدعو; وإلى شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يدعو﴾; and نكر is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شيء﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿خشعا أبصارهم يخرجون من الأجداث﴾: خشعًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in ﴿يخرجون﴾; أبصارهم is the fāʿil of the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) ﴿خشعًا﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma, and the third-person pronoun is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); يخرجون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; ومن الأجداث: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخرجون﴾; and the clause ﴿يخرجون﴾ has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.
﴿كأنهم جراد منتشر﴾: كأن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) of comparison; the third-person pronoun is in the position of the accusative as the noun of kaʾanna; جراد is the khabar (predicate) of kaʾanna, nominative with the ḍamma; منتشر: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جراد﴾; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil in ﴿يخرجون﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿مهطعين إلى الداع يقول الكافرون هذا يوم عسر﴾: مهطعين is accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), also from the fāʿil (agent) of يخرجون; وإلى الداع is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مهطعين﴾; the clause يقول الكافرون is resumptive, as if it came as an answer to a question arising from the description of the day with its terrors and of its people with their evil state; or the clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يخرجون, so the ḥāls from the wāw are then four: one placed before and three placed after; and the clause هذا يوم عسر is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح فكذبوا عبدنا وقالوا مجنون وازدجر﴾: كذبت is a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; قبلهم is an adverb (ẓarf) of time, accusative (manṣūb), by virtue of its annexation [Translator's note: so in the source, «منصوب لإضافته»], attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾; قوم نوح is the fāʿil (agent) of كذبت; فكذبوا: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and كذبوا is a verb and its fāʿil; عبدنا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); قالوا is conjoined to كذبوا; مجنون is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هو مجنون (he is a madman); وازدجر is conjoined to قالوا, i.e.: they were not content with this saying, but added to it his rebuking and repelling; and it has been said: it is conjoined to هو مجنون, so it falls within the scope of what they said, i.e.: they said: he is a madman, and he was driven away; ازدجر is a past verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فدعا ربه أني مغلوب فانتصر﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; دعا ربه is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أن with what falls in its scope is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the yāʾ is its noun, and مغلوب is its khabar (predicate); the fāʾ is conjunctive; انتصر is an imperative verb; and what انتصر is attached to (its mutaʿalliq) is omitted.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿ففتحنا أبواب السماء بماء منهمر﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, conjoining to an omitted, implied clause, i.e.: so We answered Nūḥ's supplication and opened; فتحنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أبواب السماء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وبماء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فتحنا﴾, and the bāʾ is for transitivity (al-taʿdiya), by way of hyperbole, since the water is made like the instrument with which one opens; or the bāʾ is for accompaniment (al-mulābasa), i.e.: accompanied by pouring water, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿منهمر﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ماء﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وفجرنا الأرض عيونا﴾: فجرنا is conjoined to فتحنا; الأرض is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and عيونًا is a tamyīz (specification).
﴿فالتقى الماء على أمر قد قدر﴾: فالتقى is conjoined to فجرنا; الماء is the fāʿil (agent) of التقى; وعلى أمر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) التقى, and ﴿على﴾ conveys the meaning of causation (al-taʿlīl); it has been said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause قد قدر is a naʿt (adjective) of أمر.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وحملناه على ذات ألواح ودسر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; حملناه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وعلى ذات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حملناه﴾; ألواح is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and دسر is conjoined to ألواح.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿تجري بأعيننا جزاء لمن كان كفر﴾: the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of ذات دسر, and ذات ألواح is originally a naʿt of an (omitted) سفينة (ship), so this is a second naʿt; تجري is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of its nominative is a ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ; وبأعيننا is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تجري, i.e.: guarded and protected under Our eyes; جزاء is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or it is with an implied جازيناهم جزاء (We requited them a requital), or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl; ولمن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) جزاء; and the clause كان is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿ولقد تركناها آية فهل من مدكر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); تركناها is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the pronoun refers back to the deed, which is their drowning in the manner mentioned, and it has been said: it refers back to the ship; آية is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second mafʿūl bihi if تركنا has the meaning of جعلناها (We made it); the fāʾ is conjunctive; هل is an interrogative particle; من is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and مدكر is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فكيف كان عذابي ونذر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; وكان عذابي: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, عذاب is its noun, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نذر is conjoined to عذابي, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿فكيف كان...﴾ has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر﴾: ﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw: resumptive; the lām: falling in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿يسرنا﴾ is a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿القرآن﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿للذكر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسرنا﴾; the clause ﴿لقد يسرنا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the implied oath; and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فهل من مدكر﴾: ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ: conjunctive, and هل: an interrogative particle; ﴿من﴾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and ﴿مدكر﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative in position and genitive by ﴿من﴾ in form, and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿كذبت عاد﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿فكيف كان عذابي ونذر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; وكان عذابي: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, عذاب is its noun, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نذر is conjoined to عذابي, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿إنا أرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في يوم نحس مستمر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause أرسلنا عليهم is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ريحًا is the object of أرسلنا; صرصرًا is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ريحًا﴾; and مستمر is a naʿt of النحس or of اليوم.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿تنزع الناس كأنهم أعجاز نخل منقعر﴾: the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ريحًا﴾; كأن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; أعجاز نخل is its khabar (predicate); منقعر is a naʿt of نخل; and the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿فكيف كان عذابي ونذر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; وكان عذابي: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, عذاب is its noun, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نذر is conjoined to عذابي, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر﴾: ﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw: resumptive; the lām: falling in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿يسرنا﴾ is a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿القرآن﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿للذكر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسرنا﴾; the clause ﴿لقد يسرنا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the implied oath; and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فهل من مدكر﴾: ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ: conjunctive, and هل: an interrogative particle; ﴿من﴾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and ﴿مدكر﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative in position and genitive by ﴿من﴾ in form, and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing).

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿كذبت ثمود بالنذر﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and بالنذر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فقالوا أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); أبشرًا: the hamza is interrogative, and بشرًا is accusative by al-ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun of the noun), i.e. by an implicit verb indicated by what follows it, i.e.: أنتبع بشرًا (shall we follow a human being?); منا is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بشرًا﴾; واحدًا has two possible analyses, the more apparent of which is that it is a naʿt of ﴿بشرًا﴾, except that it is problematic in that the interpreted (phrasal) adjective is placed before the explicit adjective; the answer to this is that منا in that case is not an adjective but a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿واحدًا﴾ placed before it; the second analysis is that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in نتبعه, and بشر applies to the singular and the plural; and نتبعه is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إنا إذا لفي ضلال وسعر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; إذًا is a particle of answer and requital, inoperative (muhmal); لفي: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); وفي ضلال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; and سعر is conjoined to ضلال.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿أؤلقي الذكر عليه من بيننا﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); ألقي is a past verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named); الذكر is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); وعليه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ألقي; and من بيننا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in عليه, i.e.: singled out.
﴿بل هو كذاب أشر﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject); كذاب is the khabar (predicate); and أشر is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿سيعلمون غدا من الكذاب الأشر﴾: the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying) of an omitted verb of saying, its implied form being: the Exalted said. The sīn is for the future; يعلمون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); غدًا is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعلمون﴾; من is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); الكذاب is its khabar (predicate); الأشر is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) because the interrogative stands at its head, fills the place of the two objects of يعلمون.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إنا مرسلو الناقة فتنة لهم فارتقبهم واصطبر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; مرسلو الناقة is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; فتنة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) فتنة; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); ارتقبهم is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); اصطبر is conjoined to ارتقبهم; and what ﴿واصطبر﴾ is attached to is omitted, i.e.: and be patient with their harm.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿ونبئهم أن الماء قسمة بينهم كل شرب محتضر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; نبئهم is an imperative verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being: أنت (you); the hāʾ is the first object; أن with what falls in its scope stands in the place of the second and third objects, because نبّأ takes three objects in the accusative; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الماء is its noun; قسمة is its khabar (predicate); بينهم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of قسمة, or to قسمة itself, because it has the meaning of مقسومة (divided); كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); شرب is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and محتضر is the khabar of كل.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فنادوا صاحبهم فتعاطى فعقر﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; نادوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and what it is conjoined to is omitted, i.e.: so they persisted in that; it is better that it be the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); صاحبهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فتعاطى is conjoined to فنادوا; and فعقر is conjoined to تعاطى.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿فكيف كان عذابي ونذر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an omitted clause); كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; وكان عذابي: كان is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere in this book كان is parsed as a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb], عذاب is its noun, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نذر is conjoined to عذابي, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿إنا أرسلنا عليهم صيحة واحدة فكانوا كهشيم المحتظر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause أرسلنا is its khabar (predicate); وعليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾; صيحة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); واحدة is a naʿt (adjective); فكانوا is conjoined to أرسلنا, and the wāw is the noun of kāna; ﴿كهشيم﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna; ﴿هشيم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and المحتظر is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر﴾: ﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw: resumptive; the lām: falling in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿يسرنا﴾ is a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿القرآن﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿للذكر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسرنا﴾; the clause ﴿لقد يسرنا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the implied oath; and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فهل من مدكر﴾: ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ: conjunctive, and هل: an interrogative particle; ﴿من﴾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and ﴿مدكر﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative in position and genitive by ﴿من﴾ in form, and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿كذبت قوم لوط بالنذر﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and بالنذر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿إنا أرسلنا عليهم حاصبا إلا آل لوط نجيناهم بسحر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause أرسلنا is its khabar (predicate); وعليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾; حاصبًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of exception; آل لوط is the excepted (mustathnā) by إلا. There are two views on this exception: the first is that it is connected (muttaṣil), the meaning being that He sent the storm of stones upon all of them except his family, for it was not sent upon them; the second is that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), the meaning being that it was not sent upon the family of Lūṭ; the correct view is the first. نجيناهم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and بسحر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نجيناهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿نعمة من عندنا كذلك نجزي من شكر﴾: نعمة is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), the implied form being: We bestowed upon Lūṭ and those with him a bestowal; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿من عندنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of نعمة; ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; نجزي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); من is a relative, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause شكر is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿ولقد أنذرهم بطشتنا فتماروا بالنذر﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); أنذرهم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بطشتنا is a second mafʿūl bihi, or it is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ) — two views; the fāʾ is a conjunction; تماروا is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and وبالنذر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تماروا﴾.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿ولقد راودوه عن ضيفه فطمسنا أعينهم﴾: the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause; the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿راودوه﴾ is a past verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿عن ضيفه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿راودوه﴾; ﴿فطمسنا﴾ is a past verb conjoined to ﴿راودوه﴾, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil, and ﴿أعينهم﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ is conjunctive, and what it conjoins is omitted, i.e.: so We said to them.
﴿فذوقوا عذابي ونذر﴾: the fāʾ is in the answer to an implied condition; ﴿ذوقوا﴾ is the imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; ﴿عذابي﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with a fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نذر: like ﴿عذابي﴾, and the omitted yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied condition, i.e.: if you persist in disbelief, then taste; and the whole conditional sentence is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying).

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿ولقد صبحهم بكرة عذاب مستقر﴾: also conjoined; بكرة is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صبحهم﴾, i.e.: without (it being) a specific day; عذاب is the fāʿil (agent); and مستقر is a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, i.e.: it does not leave them.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿فذوقوا عذابي ونذر﴾: the fāʾ is in the answer to an implied condition; the imperative verb is indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); عذابي is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) with a fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نذر: like عذابي, and the omitted yāʾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied condition, i.e.: if you persist in disbelief, then taste; and the whole conditional sentence is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر﴾: ﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw: resumptive; the lām: falling in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿يسرنا﴾ is a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿القرآن﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿للذكر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسرنا﴾; the clause ﴿لقد يسرنا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the implied oath; and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فهل من مدكر﴾: ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ: conjunctive, and هل: an interrogative particle; ﴿من﴾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and ﴿مدكر﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative in position and genitive by ﴿من﴾ in form, and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿ولقد جاء آل فرعون النذر﴾: ﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw: resumptive; the lām: falling in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿جاء﴾ is a past verb; ﴿آل﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فرعون﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote; ﴿النذر﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma; the clause ﴿لقد جاء﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the implied oath; and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿كذبوا بآياتنا كلها فأخذناهم أخذ عزيز مقتدر﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; كذبوا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); وبآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾; كلها is a tawkīd (emphasis) of آياتنا; فأخذناهم: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿أخذناهم﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وأخذ: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); وعزيز: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ومقتدر: a naʿt (adjective) of عزيز; and the annexation is of the type of annexing the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿أكفاركم خير من أولئكم﴾: أكفاركم: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), which has the meaning of negation; كفاركم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); خير is the khabar (predicate); and ومن أوليائكم [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the ayah is أولئكم] is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير.
﴿أم لكم براءة في الزبر﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the hamza of the interrogative of disapproval, the implied form being: بل ألكم براءة ...؟ (rather, do you have an immunity …?); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; براءة is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and ﴿في الزبر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of براءة.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿أم يقولون نحن جميع منتصر﴾: أم: disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل» plus the interrogative hamza, or meaning «بل» only; ﴿يقولون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); نحن is a mubtadaʾ (subject); جميع is the khabar (predicate); منتصر is a naʿt (adjective) of جميع, because it has the meaning of a group (jamʿ); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying); منتصر was made singular only to match the wording of ﴿جميع﴾, for it is singular in wording even though it is a noun for a group, like الرهط (band) and الجيش (army).

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿سيهزم الجمع ويولون الدبر﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future; يهزم is an imperfect verb, passive (built for the one whose agent is not named); الجمع is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); يولون is conjoined to سيهزم; and الدبر is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿بل الساعة موعدهم والساعة أدهى وأمر﴾: بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; الساعة is a mubtadaʾ (subject); موعدهم is the khabar (predicate); the wāw is a conjunction; الساعة is a mubtadaʾ; أدهى is the khabar; and أمر is conjoined to الساعة [Translator's note: so in the source; أمرّ is conjoined to أدهى]; and you may make the wāw circumstantial (of the ḥāl).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); المجرمين is its noun; وفي ضلال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); سعر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿يوم يسحبون في النار على وجوههم﴾: يوم: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of saying, i.e.: it will be said to them on the day they are dragged; the clause يسحبون is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; وفي النار is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يسحبون﴾; and وعلى وجوههم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ذوقوا مس سقر﴾: ذوقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying) of the implied verb of saying; مس is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and سقر is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); it is a proper name for Hell, and therefore it is a diptote, because it is a feminine proper name.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; كل شيء is accusative by al-ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun of the noun), by an omitted verb indicated by what follows it, i.e.: إنا خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه (We created everything; We created it); the clause of the omitted verb is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause خلقناه is explicative, with no grammatical position; and وبقدر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from كل, i.e.: measured, precise, ordered.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; ما is negating; أمرنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); واحدة is the khabar (predicate) of أمرنا; وكلمح is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from what the command relates to, namely the thing commanded to come into being, i.e.: in the state of its coming into being swiftly; and وبالبصر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to لمح.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿ولقد أهلكنا أشياعكم﴾: ﴿ولقد﴾: the wāw: resumptive; the lām: falling in the answer to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أهلكنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿أشياعكم﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the second-person pronoun is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿لقد أهلكنا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the implied oath; and the implied oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فهل من مدكر﴾: ﴿فهل﴾: the fāʾ: conjunctive, and هل: an interrogative particle; ﴿من﴾ is a redundant (ṣila) preposition; and ﴿مدكر﴾ is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: موجود (existing).

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); شيء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause فعلوه is a naʿt (adjective); and في الزبر is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿وكل صغير وكبير مستطر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); صغير is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the kasra; كبير is conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw, genitive with the kasra; مستطر is the khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma; and the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t: ﴿إن المتقين في جنات ونهر﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); المتقين is its noun; وفي جنات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); and نهر is conjoined to جنات.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿في مقعد صدق﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) of part for whole (badal baʿḍ min kull) from His words: في جنات, because the seat is part of the gardens; and you may attach it (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, as a second khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿عند مليك﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of جنات, or of مقعد; and it has been said: it is a second or third khabar of inna; مليك is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha).
﴿مقتدر﴾: a naʿt; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً: The people of tafsīr (Quranic exegesis) say: الصّرصر is the cold [wind]. Some of the people of language said: it is only called صرصر when it has a violent sound, from their saying صرّ الشيء when a thing makes a sound; the origin is صرر, and one of the rāʾs was replaced by a ṣād. فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ: Some of the people of tafsīr said: النحس means "severe". Had it been as he said, يوم would have taken tanwīn (nunation) and it would have been said نحس [as an adjective], not in a genitive construct.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
تَنْزِعُ النَّاسَ: It was said: it plucked them out of the pits which they had dug. كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ: النخل (palm trees) is treated as masculine and as feminine; these are two dialects, and the Qur'an has brought both. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] claimed that there is an ellipsis in the wording and that the meaning is: "it plucks people out and leaves them like the trunks of palm trees." He said: on this view the kāf would be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by the omitted verb. But this does not need the ellipsis he spoke of. The correct view on it is what Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said; he said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. it plucks people out [while they are] like palm trees uprooted, i.e. in this state. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is the true i'rab; if one takes the meaning loosely, then the meaning comes back to what Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said.

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related: When the wind rose, a group of seven men of ʿĀd stood up, lined up at the entrance of the ravine, and blocked the wind from the women and children who were in the ravine. The wind then came in from underneath them one by one, uprooted each, turned him over onto his head and broke his neck, until it had destroyed six, and one remained, called al-Khaljān. He came to Hūd ﷺ and said: "What are these that I see like Bactrian camels beneath the clouds?" He said: "These are the angels, peace be upon them." He said: "If I accept Islam, what do I get?" He said: "You will be safe." He said: "Will your Lord grant me retaliation against those who are in the clouds?" He said: "Woe to you! Have you ever seen a king grant retaliation against his own troops?" He said: "Even if He did, I would not be content." He [the narrator] said: So he went back to his place and began to recite: [rajaz metre] 443-
لم يبق إلّا الخلجان نفسه ... يا شرّ يوم قد دهاني أمسه
(None is left but al-Khaljān himself; O worst of days, whose evening has struck me!)
Then there befell him what had befallen his companions, and they became as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ.

Mujāhid said about their being likened to the trunks of uprooted palm trees: it is because their bodies had been separated from their heads, so they became bodies without heads. One of the people of speculative reasoning said: the comparison is to the pits in which they had been standing; the pits became like the trunks of palm trees. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is an erroneous one. Had it been as he said, it would have been كأنّها or كأنّهن; moreover, the pits have not been mentioned before so as to be referred to by a pronoun. Moreover, the comparison to the people is more fitting, especially as it is the view of one whose word is taken as proof.

nahhas-irab:21-22.t: فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ (21): i.e. how was My punishment of them for unbelief, and My warning you that what befell them may befall you? Abū Isḥāq said: نذر is the plural of نذير.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ (23): ثمود is not declined as a triptote because it is the name of the tribe; it may be declined fully as being the name of the clan (ḥayy).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا واحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ: You put بشرا in the accusative by an implied verb, and the meaning is: "Shall we follow a single human being from among us, while we are a multitude?" إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ: i.e. in confusion away from the straight path and taking a crooked course. إذن does not govern when the speech does not rest upon it. وَسُعُرٍ may be the plural of سعير, or a maṣdar (verbal noun) from their saying سعر الرجل when a man becomes rash and frenzied.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنا: an interrogative containing the sense of rebuke (tawqīf). بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ: The Kufans say «بل» only comes after a negation, so they interpret the like of this according to the meaning, because the meaning of "was the Reminder sent down upon him?" is "it was not sent down upon him."

nahhas-irab:26-27.t:
سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً: The origin [of غد] according to Sībawayh is غدو; the wāw was dropped from it. مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), [the clause being] in the position of the accusative governed by سيعلمون. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it as ستعلمون غدا ("you will know tomorrow"), while Abū ʿUbayd inclines to the reading with yāʾ because after it comes إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ, and He did not say "for you" (لكم). Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied construction for whoever reads with yāʾ is: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً [Translator's note: so in the printed text; since the discussion answers the objection to the tāʾ reading, the intended sense may be the reading with tāʾ, with an implied "saying" before the second-person address], and "saying" is frequently omitted.

The origin is إنّا مرسلون; the nūn was dropped for lightness and [مرسلو] was put in construct [with الناقة]. فتنة لهم: Abū Isḥāq said: فتنة is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Someone else said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. We tried them with that and tested them. Their trial in it was that the she-camel came out for them from a solid rock — a huge she-camel — and some of them believed. Because of her size she ate a great deal, so they complained of that to Ṣāliḥ ﷺ and said: "She has finished off the grasses and herbs and kept us from the water."
