4155 - بدِجلَةَ دارُهُمْ ولقد أَرَاهُمْ ... بدِجْلةَ مُهْطِعين إلى السَّماع
(Their abode is on the Tigris, and I used to see them on the Tigris, hastening to the audition.)
It was said: hurrying with the neck stretched out. It was also said: looking. And a verse was quoted:
4156 - تَعَبَّدَني نِمْرُ بنُ سَعْدٍ وقد أُرَى ... ونِمْرُ بنُ سَعْدٍ لي مُطيعٌ ومُهْطِعُ
(Nimr ibn Saʿd enslaved me, though I used to be seen, when Nimr ibn Saʿd was obedient and hastening to me.)
The discussion of this root was given in sūrat Ibrāhīm.
His saying: {يَقُولُ الكافرون}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُهْطعين». There is something to consider in it, in that the clause lacks a link tying it to the owner of the ḥāl. It may be answered that «الكافرون» are the pronoun in meaning, so it is a case of linking by the overt noun, according to those who allow this, as if it were said 'they say this'. He made them explicit only to denounce them with this ugly description."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ}: its object is omitted, that is: "they denied the messengers", because when they denied Nūḥ, peace be upon him, they denied all the messengers. It is not allowed that the question be a case of tanāzuʿ (rival governance); for if it were, the implied form would be: "the people of Nūḥ denied before them our servant, and they denied him", and if this were pronounced, it would be emphasis, since it would add nothing beyond the first. The condition of tanāzuʿ is that the second not be emphasis, so they prevented the following saying from being such:
4175 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أتاكِ أتاكِ اللاحقون احْبِسِ احبسِ
(… They have come to you, they have come to you, the pursuers: hold back, hold back!) [Translator's note: the verse number 4175 is as in the source, out of sequence with the surrounding numbers.]
In al-Zamakhsharī's words there is something that allows it, for he took it out of emphasis. He said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying «فكذَّبوا» after His saying «كَذَّبَتْ»? I say: its meaning is 'they denied, so they denied our servant', that is: they denied him, denial following denial, whenever a denying generation passed away from them, another denying generation followed it." This is a good meaning that allows tanāzuʿ. And «مجنون» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "he is mad". The dāl in «ازْدُجِر» is a substitute for tāʾ, as above. Is it part of what they said, that is: they said that he was driven away (izdujira), meaning the jinn drove him away and took away his mind; Mujāhid said this; or is it Allah the Exalted's speech, reporting about him that he was rebuked and driven off with abuse and kinds of harm?

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ}: the majority read with fatḥa on the hamza, that is: "he called upon Him with 'that I am overcome'"; this came as a report of the meaning, and had it come as a report of the wording, he would have said «إنه مغلوبٌ»; both are allowed. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash read it, and it is also transmitted from ʿĀṣim, with kasra: either by an implied "saying", that is "so he said", explaining the prayer by it, which is the view of the Basrans; or by treating the prayer like saying, which is the view of the Kufans. The disagreement about «فَتَحْنا» was given in al-Anʿām, and praise be to Allah.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {مُّنْهَمِرٍ}: al-munhamir: abundant, descending with force. A verse was quoted:
4158 - راحَ تَمْرِيْه الصَّبا ثم انتحى ... فيه شُؤْبُوْبُ جَنوبٍ مُنْهَمِرْ
(It set out, the east wind drawing it forth; then there turned upon it a downpour from the south, streaming.)
It was used figuratively in their saying hamara al-rajul fī kalāmihi, and fulān yuhāmiru al-shayʾ, that is: he sweeps it away; and hamarahu min mālihi: he gave him much.
There are two views on the bāʾ in «بماء». The more apparent: that it is for transitivity, and that is by way of intensification, in that He made the water like the instrument by which it is opened, as you say "I opened with the key". The second: that it is for the ḥāl, that is: "We opened them accompanied by this water". ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «وفَجَرْنا» lightened, while the rest read it with shadda.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {عُيُوناً}: There are several views on it; the most famous: that it is a tamyīz (specification), that is: "We made the springs of the earth gush forth", so he shifted it from being an object to being a tamyīz, as it is shifted from being an agent.
Some prevented this and interpreted this verse according to what will come: {وَفَجَّرْنَا الأرض عُيُوناً} is more emphatic than «فَجَّرْنا عيونَ الأرض», for what was mentioned in its parallel more than once. Two: that it is accusative as a badal of «الأرض». What weakens this is that it has no pronoun, for it is a badal of a part from the whole. This is answered by saying that it is omitted, that is: "springs from it", as in {الأخدود النار} [al-Burūj: 4-5], where «النار» is a badal of inclusion and there is no pronoun, so it is implied. Three: that it is a second object because «فَجَّرنا» is made to include the meaning "We turned it, by causing it to gush, into springs". Four: that it is a ḥāl. In this are two figurative stretches: the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "possessing springs", and its being an anticipated ḥāl rather than a concurrent one.
His saying: {فَالْتَقَى المآء}: since by "water" the genus is meant, it is right to say "the water met", as if: the water of the sky and the water of the earth met. This is the reading of the majority. Al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb read, and it is also transmitted from the Commander of the Believers, «الماءان» in the dual, with the hamza intact. Al-Ḥasan also read «الماوان», turning it into a wāw. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "like their saying ʿilbāwān", meaning that he likened the hamza turned from hāʾ to the hamza of ilḥāq. It is also reported from him «المايان» with it turned into a yāʾ, which is stronger than the previous one.
And His saying: {قَدْ قُدِرَ}: the majority read it lightened. Ibn Miqsam and Abū Ḥaywa read it with shadda, and they are two dialectal forms read in both ways: His saying {قَدَّرَ فهدى} [al-Aʿlā: 3], {قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ} [al-Ṭalāq: 7], as will come.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ}: that is: a ship possessing planks. Al-Zamakhsharī said: it is among the adjectives that stand in the place of the described nouns, taking their place and performing their function, so that nothing separates the one from the other. Similar is:
4159 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ولكنْ ... نَ قميصي مَسْرودةٌ مِنْ حديدِ
(… but my shirt is one of chain-mail made of iron.) He meant: "but my shirt is a coat of mail". Likewise:
4160 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولو في عيونِ النازياتِ بأَكْرُعِ
(… even in the eyes of the leapers, on legs.) He meant: "even in the eye of the locust". Do you not see that if you combined the ship with these descriptions, or the eyes of the locust and the coat of mail with these two descriptions, it would not be correct? This is among eloquent and wondrous speech. As for al-dusur, there are several views: one, that they are nails, the plural of disār, like kutub as plural of kitāb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "the plural of disār, which is a nail, on the pattern fiʿāl, from dasarahu when he pushed it, because its passage is pushed with it." Al-Rāghib said: "the singular is dasr", meaning that it is like saqf and suqf. The basic sense of al-dasr is a hard push by force; dasarahu bi-l-rumḥ (he thrust him with a spear); and midsar is like miṭʿan. It is reported: "There is no zakāt in ambergris; it is only something that the sea has pushed out (dasarahu)", that is: thrust out. Two: that they are the threads with which ships are tied. Three: that they are the cross-pieces of the ship. Four: that they are its ribs.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {بِأَعْيُنِنَا}: that is: "accompanied by Our protection", and it is in meaning like His saying {وَلِتُصْنَعَ على عيني} [Ṭāhā: 39]. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Abū al-Sammāl read «بأَعْيُنَّا» with assimilation.
His saying: {جَزَآءً}: accusative as mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), made accusative by «فَفَتْحْنا» and what follows. It was also said: accusative as a maṣdar, either by an implied verb, that is: "We requited them with a requital", or figuratively, in that the meaning of the preceding actions is "We requited them by them with a requital".
His saying: {لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ}: the majority read «كُفِرَ», passive, and by "the one who was denied" is meant Nūḥ, peace be upon him, or the Creator the Exalted. Maslama ibn Muḥārib read «كُفْر» with sukūn on the fāʾ, as in the saying:
4161 - لو عُصْرَ منه المِسْكُ والبانُ انعصَرْ ...
(Were musk and ban-wood squeezed from him, they would be squeezed out.)
Yazīd ibn Rūmān, ʿĪsā and Qatāda read «كَفَر», active, and by «مَنْ» then are meant the people of Nūḥ. And «كُفِرَ» is the khabar of kāna. In it is evidence that the khabar of kāna may be in the past without «قد», though some say that «قد» is required, overt or implied. It is also possible that «كان» is redundant. The pronoun of «تَرَكْناها» is either for the story, or for the deed, or for the ship, which is the apparent sense.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {مُّدَّكِرٍ}: its origin is mudhtakir; the tāʾ was changed into an undotted dāl, then the dotted (dhāl) was changed into an undotted one for their closeness. This was given in His saying {وادكر بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ} [Yūsuf: 45]. «مُذْتكِر» has also been read on this original form. Qatāda, in what Abū al-Faḍl reports from him, read «مُذَكِّر» with fatḥa on the dhāl, lightened, and shadda on the kāf, from dhakkara with shadda, that is: he reminded himself or another of the past stories of the ancients. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from him like the group, except with the dotted dhāl, and it is irregular, because the first is changed to the second, not the second to the first.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي}: the apparent sense is that «كان» is incomplete (nāqiṣa), so «كيف» is a fronted khabar. It was also said that it may be complete (tāmma), in which case «كيف» is in the position of accusative, either as a time-adverbial or as a ḥāl, as was verified in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
The meaning of "We have made the Qurʾān easy (yassarnā)" is: We prepared it for remembrance, from their saying yassara farasahu, that is: he prepared it for riding by bridling it. The poet said:
4162 - فَقُمتُ إليه باللِّجام مُيَسَّراً ... هنالك يَجْزِيني الذي كنتُ أصنع
(I rose to it with the bridle, made ready; there it repays me for what I used to do.)

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {صَرْصَراً}: that is, one of intense sound, from ṣarṣara al-bāb or al-qalam when it makes a sound; or one of intense cold, from al-ṣirr, which is cold. All of these are original roots according to the majority. Makkī said: "Its origin is ṣarrara, from ṣarra al-bāb when it makes a sound, but they replaced the doubled rāʾ with ṣād." I (al-Samīn) say: This is the view of the Kufans. Like it are kabkaba and kafkafa, and this was given in Fuṣṣilat and elsewhere.
His saying: {يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ}: the majority read with the annexation of «يوم» to «نَحْس» with sukūn on the ḥāʾ. There are two views on it. One: that it is an annexation of the described to its description. The second, which is the view of the Basrans: that it is an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is: "a day of ill-omened punishment". Al-Ḥasan read with its tanwīn, describing it with «نَحْس»; al-Zamakhsharī did not specify the kasra on the ḥāʾ, but the Shaykh did. His saying the Exalted {في أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ} [Fuṣṣilat: 16] was read with sukūn and kasra on the ḥāʾ. The tanwīn of «أيام» is according to all, as was established. And «ومُسْتمر» is an adjective of «يوم» or of «نَحْسٍ», and its meaning is as above, that is: it continued upon them until it destroyed them, or from bitterness.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
And «تَنْزِعُ» is in the position of accusative, either as an adjective of «ريحاً» or as a ḥāl from it, since it is specified by the adjective; it may also be resumptive. He said «الناس» to include their males and females, so he put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun for that reason; otherwise the original is «تَنْزِعُهم».
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ}: an anticipated ḥāl from al-nās. And «مُنْقَعِر» is an adjective of «نَخْلٍ» taking the genus into account; had it been made feminine, the meaning of a group would have been considered, as in {نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 7]; the verification of the two usages has been given. He made it masculine here and feminine in al-Ḥāqqa out of regard for the verse endings in the two places. Abū Nahīk read «أَعْجُزُ» on the pattern afʿul, like ḍabuʿ and aḍbuʿ. It was said: the kāf is in the position of accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "so He left them as though they were trunks"; Makkī said this. If it were made a second object by inclusion of meaning, that is: "He turns them by uprooting into what are like…", it would be nearer.
Al-aʿjāz: plural of ʿajuz, which is the back of a thing; from it comes al-ʿajz (incapacity), because it leads to the lagging of affairs. Al-munqaʿir: uprooted from its base; qaʿartu al-nakhla: I uprooted it from its base, so it was uprooted. Qaʿartu al-biʾr: I reached its bottom. Qaʿartu al-ināʾ: I drank what was in it until I reached its bottom; and aqʿartu al-biʾr, that is: I made a bottom for it; and qaʿartuhā: I reached its bottom.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {أَبَشَراً}: accusative by ishtighāl (pre-occupation), which is the preferred view, because an interrogative particle, which is more fitting for a verb, precedes it; «ومِنَّا» is an adjective of it. And «واحداً» has two views. The more apparent: that it is an adjective of «بَشَراً», but a difficulty arises in that the interpreted description precedes the explicit one. The answer is that «مِنَّا» is then not a description but a ḥāl from «واحداً», put before it. The second: that it is accusative as ḥāl from the hāʾ of «نَتَّبِعُه», and this is an escape from the preceding analysis. But what favours its being an adjective is the reading of the two in the nominative: «أبَشرٌ مِنا واحد نَتَّبِعُهُ», as will come; this favours «واحداً» being an adjective of «بشراً», not a ḥāl. Abū al-Sammāl read, in what al-Hudhalī and al-Dānī report, both in the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «واحدٌ» its adjective and «نَتَّبعهُ» its khabar. Abū al-Sammāl also read, in what Ibn Khālawayh, Abū al-Faḍl and Ibn ʿAṭiyya report, «بَشَرٌ» in the nominative and «واحداً» in the accusative, and there are several views on it. One: that «أبَشَرٌ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, its implied form being: "a human being from among us, sent to us or dispatched". As for the accusative of «واحداً», there are two views: one, that it is a ḥāl from the hāʾ… [Translator's note: the source text is garbled here; the sentence breaks off and continues with «بالابتداءِ أيضاً», "by ibtidāʾ also"], and the khabar is «نَتَّبِعُه», and «واحداً» is a ḥāl according to the two views mentioned above. Three: that it is nominative by an implied passive verb, its implied form being: "Is a human being informed?", with «مِنَّا» an adjective and «واحداً» a ḥāl too according to the two views mentioned above. Ibn ʿAṭiyya took this view.
His saying: {وَسُعُرٍ}: it may be singular, that is: madness. One says nāqa masʿūra, that is: like a mad one in her going. The poet said:
4163 - كأنَّ بها سُعْراً إذا العِيْسُ هَزَّها ... ذَمِيْلٌ وإرْخاءٌ من السير متعبُ
(As if she had madness when the white camels are urged on by a brisk pace and a loose, tiring gait.)
And it may be the plural of saʿīr, which is fire; both possibilities are transmitted.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {مِن بَيْنِنَا}: a ḥāl from the hāʾ of «عليه», that is: "was cast upon him, singled out from among us".
His saying: {أَشِرٌ}: al-ashir: the insolently exultant. One says ashira yaʾshar asharan, so he is ashir like fariḥ, and āshir like ḍārib, and ashrān like sakrān, and ushārā like sukārā. Abū Qilāba read, making them both afʿal of comparison. You say "Zayd is khayr than ʿAmr and sharr than Bakr"; and we do not say akhyar nor ashar except rarely, as in this reading and as in the saying of Ruʾba:
4164 - بِلالُ خيرُ الناسِ وابنُ الأَخْيَرِ ...
(Bilāl is the best of people and the son of the best.)
And they are established in both in the exclamation of wonder, such as mā akhyarahu and mā asharrahu. And it is not dropped except rarely, the reverse of afʿal of comparison. They said: "mā khayra al-laban lil-ṣaḥīḥ wa-mā sharrahu lil-mabṭūn" ("how good milk is for the healthy and how bad for the one with a stomach complaint"); and this is among the beauties of the craft. Abū Qays al-Awdī and Mujāhid read the second word «الأُشُرُ» with three ḍammas. Its explanation is that there is a dialect «أَشُر» with ḍamma on the shīn, like ḥadhur and ḥadhir, then the hamza was given ḍamma according to the principle of that dialect, like ḥadhur.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {فِتْنَةً}: an object of purpose, or a maṣdar from the meaning of the first, or in the position of ḥāl.

semin-durr:28-28.t: The majority read «قِسْمَةٌ» with kasra on the qāf. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr that he read it with fatḥa, which is the analogy for the single occurrence. The pronoun in «بَيْنَهم» is for the people of Ṣāliḥ and the she-camel, and he gave precedence to the rational.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {فَنَادَوْاْ}: before it something is omitted, that is: "they persisted in that, then grew tired of it and resolved to hamstring her, so they called their companion". And taʿāṭā is the reciprocal of ʿāṭā, as if they were passing it back and forth until the most wretched of them took it upon himself.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {كَهَشِيمِ المحتظر}: the majority read with kasra on the ẓāʾ, an active participle, which is the one who makes an enclosure (ḥaẓīra) from firewood and the like. Abū al-Sammāl, Abū Ḥaywa, Abū Rajāʾ and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read it with fatḥa. It was said: it is a maṣdar, that is: "like the chaff of enclosure-making". It was also said: it is a place. It was also said: it is a passive participle, being the chaff itself, and it would be a case of annexation of the described to its description, like masjid al-jāmiʿ. Al-ḥaẓr: prevention, and its verification was given in sūrat Subḥān.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ آلَ لُوطٍ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is continuous, and the meaning is that He sent the pelting stones upon all except his family, upon whom He did not send them. The second: that it is discontinuous, and I do not know what its explanation is, for discontinuity and its absence are an expression for the excepted not being included in that from which it is excepted, and this is included, nothing else. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a discontinuous exception. It was also said: continuous, because the pelting stones were sent upon all of them and they perished except the family of Lūṭ. On the first view, the stones were not sent upon the family of Lūṭ." End of quotation. This is a problematic statement.
And His saying: {نَّجَّيْنَاهُم}: an explanation and an answer to someone who says: "What was the case of the family of Lūṭ?", like «أبى» after His saying {إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ} [al-Baqara: 34], which was discussed in al-Baqara.
«وبسَحَرٍ»: the bāʾ is for ḥāl or locative. «سَحَر» is fully declined because it is indefinite; had a particular time been intended by it, it would be diptote because of definiteness and deviation from «al-»; this is the well-known view. Ṣadr al-Afāḍil claimed that it is indeclinable with fatḥa, like amsi indeclinable with kasra.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {نِّعْمَةً}: either a direct object, or a maṣdar of a verb from its own wording, or from the meaning of «نَجَّيْناهم», because saving them is a favour; so the interpretation is either in the operator or in the maṣdar. «ومِنْ عندِنا»: either attached to «نعمة», or to an omitted adjective of it. The kāf in «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "We requite with a requital like that". The majority read «فَطَمَسْنا» lightened. Ibn Miqsam read it with shadda, for multiplicity, because of what it relates to or because of the severity of the act in itself.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {بُكْرَةً}: fully declined because it is indefinite; had a particular time been intended by it, it would be diptote because of definiteness and feminine gender. This is as was said before about «غُدْوة». Zayd ibn ʿAlī made it diptote, taking it to be a particular time.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ}: a maṣdar annexed to its agent.

semin-durr:44-44.t: And {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ}: the majority read in the third person, as an iltifāt (shift of person). Abū Ḥaywa, Abū al-Barhasam and Mūsā al-Aswārī read in the second person, following what came before in «أكُفَّاركم» to the end.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
The majority read «سَيُهْزَمُ» passive, and «والجَمْعُ» is nominative by it. «ستَهْزِمُ» was also read, with fatḥa on the tāʾ, addressed to the Messenger, peace be upon him, with «الجمعَ» as direct object. Abū Ḥaywa in one transmission, and Yaʿqūb, read «سَنَهْزِمُ» with the nūn of the one who magnifies himself, and «الجمعَ» is also accusative. It is also reported from Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla «سَيَهْزِمُ» with the yāʾ of the third person, active, «الجمعَ» accusative, that is: "Allah will defeat the host". As for «ويُوَلُّون», the majority read in the third person. Abū Ḥaywa and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «وتُوَلُّون» with the tāʾ of address, and it is clear.
And al-dubur here is a generic noun. It is fitting here because it occurs as a verse ending, unlike {لَيُوَلُّنَّ الأدبار} [al-Ḥashr: 12]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is: al-adbār, as he said: 4166 - كُلُوا في بَعْضِ بَطْنِكُمُ تَعِفُّوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Eat in part of your belly and you will be chaste …)
«الإِدْبار» was also read." The Shaykh said: "It is not like «بعضِ بَطْنكم», because the singular here has something that makes it good, whereas nothing makes the singular of «بَطْنكم» good."

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {ذُوقُواْ}: with an intended "saying". Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of Maḥbūb from him, read «مَسَّقَر», and Ibn Mujāhid called it a mistake. He is to be excused, because the last sīn of «مَسَّ» is itself assimilated into, so it is not assimilated into another, since whenever something is assimilated into it, it must have a vowel, and whenever it is assimilated, it must be sākin, so the combination of the two conflicts. The Shaykh said: "The assumption about Abū ʿAmr is that he did not assimilate until he dropped one of the two letters, because of the meeting of like letters, and then assimilated." I (al-Samīn) say: Ibn Mujāhid's words concern what they said, that he assimilated; but if he dropped and assimilated, there is no difficulty.
«وسَقَر» is a proper name for Jahannam, may Allah protect us from it, derived from saqarathu al-shams wa-l-nār, that is: it scorched him; and one says ṣaqarathu with ṣād, which is substituted for sīn because of the qāf. Dhū al-Rumma said: 4167 - إذا ذابتِ الشمسُ اتَّقى صَقَراتِها ... بأَفْنانِ مَرْبوع الصَّريمةِ مُعْبِلِ
(When the sun melts, he guards against its scorching with the branches of a sturdy-resolved, long-haired one.)
«وسَقَر» is necessarily diptote, because the vowel of the middle letter takes the place of a fourth letter, like ʿaqrab and Zaynab.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ}: the majority read «كل» accusative by ishtighāl, and Abū al-Sammāl read it nominative. People have preferred the accusative, indeed some have made it obligatory. He said: because the nominative suggests what is not allowed by the principles of Ahl al-Sunna. That is, if «كل شيء» is nominative it is a mubtadaʾ, «وخَلَقْناه» is an adjective of «كل» or of «شيء», and «بقَدَر» is its khabar. In that case it has a mafhūm (implied sense) which is not hidden from one who reflects on it, so it follows that a thing not created by Allah the Exalted is not by decree; so some have worked it out. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The accusative is preferable because it indicates the generality of creation, whereas the nominative does not indicate its generality, but only gives that every created thing is by decree." Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "The preferred choice according to the principles of the Basrans was the nominative of «كل», just as the preferred choice according to them in your saying «زيدٌ ضربْتُه» is the nominative, while the preferred choice according to the Kufans there is the accusative, unlike our saying «زيد أكرمتُه», because something that operates on what follows has preceded in the verse, namely «إنَّ», and the preferred choice according to them is the accusative in it. The readers agreed on the accusative for «كل» by the choice of the Kufans, in order to indicate the generality of created things: that they belong to Allah the Exalted, unlike what the people of deviation said, that there are created things belonging to other than Allah the Exalted. The accusative of «كلَّ» indicates generality only because the implied form is: 'Indeed We created every thing We created, by decree'; so «خَلَقْناه» is emphasis and explanation of the implied «خَلَقْنا» that makes «كلَّ» accusative. If you omit it and show the first, the implied form becomes: 'Indeed We created every thing by decree', which is a general expression covering all created things. It is not allowed that «خَلَقْناه» be an adjective of «شيءٍ», because the adjective and the ṣila do not operate on what precedes the described or the relative noun, and neither is an explanation of what operates on what precedes it. So when «خَلَقْناه» cannot remain an adjective, nothing remains except that it is emphasis and explanation of the implied accusative, and that indicates generality. Also the accusative is the preferred choice because «إنَّا» according to them seeks a verb, so it is more fitting for it; thus the accusative in «كل» is the preferred choice according to them, and when to it is added the meaning of generality and exit from doubts, the accusative was better than the nominative."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "A group of Ahl al-Sunna (read) with the nominative." Abū al-Fatḥ said: "It is the preferred way in Arabic, but our reading is with the accusative along with the group." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«كلَّ شيء» is accusative by an implied verb that the overt one explains. «كلُّ شيءٍ» was also read nominative. Al-qadr and al-qadar: measuring, and both were read, that is: We created everything measured, firmly made, arranged according to what wisdom required, or measured, written in the Tablet, known before its coming to be, for We knew its state and its time." End of quotation. Here he did not take the side of the Muʿtazila, because of the weakness of the nominative reading.
A group said: when the verb is suspected to be an adjective and what follows it could serve as the khabar, and the meaning requires the verb to be the khabar, the accusative is chosen for the first noun so that it becomes clear that the verb is not an adjective; and this place is of that kind, because the nominative reading suggests that the verb is an adjective and that the khabar is «بقدَر». Ahl al-Sunna and the Qadariyya have disputed over using this verse as evidence. Ahl al-Sunna say: everything is created by Allah the Exalted by decree, and their proof is the accusative reading, because in this construction nothing is explained except what could be a khabar if the first were made nominative as a mubtadaʾ. The Qadariyya say: the reading is with the nominative of «كل», with «خَلَقْناه» in the position of adjective of «كل», that is: "Our matter or affair is: everything We created is by a decree or measure, within the limit of its form and its time."
Some scholars said: there are several aspects of «القَدَر» here. One: that it is the measure in its essence and attributes. Two: measuring, as in {فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ القادرون} [al-Mursalāt: 23]. The poet said: 4168 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقَد قَدَّر الرحمنُ ما هو قادِرُ (… and the Merciful has decreed what He decrees.) that is: what is decreed. Three: al-qadar that is said together with al-qaḍāʾ, as in your saying "it was by the decree (qaḍāʾ) of Allah and His qadar". So «بقَدَرٍ» on the accusative reading is attached to the verb that makes it accusative, and on the nominative reading it is in the position of nominative, because it is the khabar of «كل», and «كل» with its khabar is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ».

semin-durr:52-52.t: Shortly there will come a verse that is the reverse of this, I mean in the choice of the nominative, which is His saying {وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِي الزبر}, for there is no disagreement about its being nominative. They said: because making it accusative would lead to corruption of the meaning, as what actually occurs is the opposite. That is, if you made it accusative, the implied form would be: "they did everything in the Scrolls", which is contrary to fact, since in the Scrolls there are very many things they did not do. The nominative reading yields that everything they did is established in the Scrolls, and that is what is intended; therefore it was agreed to make it nominative. These two places are among the subtleties of the Arabic questions that happen to come in one sūra in two nearby places, and among the things that show the majesty of the science of iʿrāb and its making understood of subtle meanings. And the ignorant are enemies of the people of knowledge.

semin-durr:53-53.t: The majority read «مُسْتَطَرٌ» with the tāʾ lightened, from al-saṭr, which is writing, that is: written down. Al-Aʿmash and ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr read it, and it is also reported from ʿĀṣim, with the tāʾ doubled. There are two views on it. One: that it is derived from ṭarra al-shārib and al-nabāt, that is: it appeared and sprouted, meaning that everything, little or much, is manifest in the Tablet, not hidden; so its pattern is mustafʿal like mustakhraj. The second: that it is from istiṭār, like the reading of the majority, and the rāʾ was doubled only because of pausing, as in their saying "hādhā Jaʿfarr and Faraj", and then continuous reading was made to follow pausing; so its pattern is muftaʿal, like the reading of the majority.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {نَهَرٍ}: the majority read it in the singular, and it is a generic noun, as shown by its being paired with the plural; the hāʾ has fatḥa, which is the eloquent form. Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, Abū al-Sammāl and al-Fayyāḍ gave it sukūn, and it is a minor dialect; its discussion was given at the beginning of al-Baqara. It was said that what is meant here is not a river of water, but rather broad provision, since the root indicates that, as in the saying of Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm:
4169 - مَلَكْتُ بها كَفِّي فَأَنْهَرْتُ فَتْقَها ... يَرى قائمٌ مِنْ دونِها ما وراءَها
(With it I wielded my hand and widened its rent; one standing on this side of it sees what lies beyond.)
that is: I widened. Abū Nahīk, Abū Mijlaz, al-Aʿmash and Zuhayr al-Furqubī read «ونُهُر» with ḍamma on the nūn and the hāʾ, and it admits two views. One: that it is a plural of nahar with vowel on the hāʾ, which is preferable, like usud for asad. The second: that it is a plural of the form with sukūn, like suqf for saqf and ruhun for rahn; and the plural suits the plural before it, in «جنات». The reading of the majority in the singular is more emphatic. The statement of Ibn ʿAbbās was already given at the end of al-Baqara, in His saying {وملائكته وَكُتُبِهِ} [al-Baqara: 285] in the singular, and that it is more than «الكتب». Also al-Zamakhsharī's explanation of that was given, so refer to it …
His saying the Exalted {فِي مَقْعَدِ}: it may be a second khabar, which is the apparent sense, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase because it occurs as khabar. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be a badal of His saying «في جنات»; in that case it may be a badal of a part, since the seat is part of them, or of inclusion, as they include it; the first is more apparent. The majority read «مَقْعَد» in the singular, meaning the genus, as given for «نَهَر». ʿUthmān al-Battī read «مقاعِدِ», which suits the plural before it. And «مَقْعَدُ صِدْقٍ» is of the type rajul ṣidq: it may be an annexation of the described to its description. And ṣidq may be meant as the opposite of lying, that is: they were told the truth in the report of it; or it may be meant as excellence and goodness.
And «مليك» is an intensive form and suits this place. It should not be imagined that its origin is malik because that is what occurs in other places, and that the kasra was lengthened and a yāʾ arose from it; for lengthening does not occur except by necessity or rarely, even though it occurred in Hishām's reading «أَفْئِيدَةً» at the end of Ibrāhīm, where you should consult what I mentioned there.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فَانْتَصِرْ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنِّي): it is read with fatḥa, i.e. "that I am" (بِأَنِّي); and with kasra, because «دَعَا» has the meaning of "said".

ukberi-tibyan:12-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا فَالْتَقَى الْمَاءُ عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ (١٢) وَحَمَلْنَاهُ عَلَى ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ (١٣) تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنَا جَزَاءً لِمَنْ كَانَ كُفِرَ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَالْتَقَى الْمَاءُ): He meant the two waters, but sufficed with the singular because it is a generic noun.
And (عَلَى أَمْرٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an adverb (ẓarf).
The hāʾ in «حَمَلْنَاهُ» is for Noah, peace be upon him.
And (تَجْرِي) is an adjective (ṣifa) in the position of the genitive. And (بِأَعْيُنِنَا) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «تَجْرِي», i.e. "protected".
And (جَزَاءً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or on the implied wording "We recompensed them". And (كُفِرَ), i.e. "was disbelieved in", namely Noah, peace be upon him. It is also read «كَفَرَ» with the agent named, i.e. the disbeliever.

ukberi-tibyan:15-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْنَاهَا آيَةً فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ (١٥) فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ (١٦)).
And (مُدَّكِرٍ) is with dāl; its origin is dhāl and tāʾ, and it has been discussed in Yūsuf. It is also read with a doubled dhāl, which has also been discussed.
(وَنُذُرِ) means "warning" (إِنْذَار); it is also said that the implied wording is وَنُذُرِي ("and My warnings").

ukberi-tibyan:19-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ (١٩) تَنْزِعُ النَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ (٢٠)).
And (مُسْتَمِرٍّ) is a naʿt (adjective) of نَحْس; it is also said: of يَوْم.
And (كَأَنَّهُمْ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «مُنْقَعِرٍ» is a naʿt of نَخْل, which is treated as masculine and as feminine.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَالُوا أَبَشَرًا مِنَّا وَاحِدًا نَتَّبِعُهُ إِنَّا إِذًا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ وَسُعُرٍ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَبَشَرًا) is accusative by a verb explained by the one mentioned, i.e. "shall we follow a human being?", and «مِنَّا» is a naʿt (adjective). It is also read «أَبَشَرٌ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِنَّا» being its naʿt. And (وَاحِدًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «نَتَّبِعُهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَؤُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنَا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَيْنِنَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, i.e. "upon him alone". And (أَشِرٌ) with kasra on the shīn and with ḍamma are two dialects, like فَرِحٌ and فَرُحٌ.
It is also read with a doubled rāʾ (أَشَرُّ), as afʿal from الشَّرّ ("evil"); this is anomalous (shādhdh).

ukberi-tibyan:27-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا مُرْسِلُو النَّاقَةَ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ وَاصْطَبِرْ (٢٧) وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْمَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ (٢٨)).
(فِتْنَةً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (قِسْمَةٌ) means "divided" (مَقْسُوم).

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَّبُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْوَاءَهُمْ وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (مُسْتَقِرٌّ) is its khabar (predicate).
It is also read with fatḥa on the qāf (مُسْتَقَرٌّ), i.e. "settled upon"; it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الِاسْتِقْرَار.
It is also read in the genitive (مُسْتَقِرٍّ) as an adjective (ṣifa) of أَمْر; and regarding «كُلُّ» there are two views.
First: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "is acted upon" or "has come".
Second: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السَّاعَةِ».

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَكَانُوا كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ): it is read with kasra on the ẓāʾ, i.e. "like the dry stubble of the man who makes the trees into an enclosure". It is also read with fatḥa on it, i.e. "like the dry stubble of the trees taken as an enclosure". It is also said that it (the fatḥa form) means "the making of an enclosure" (الِاحْتِظَار).

ukberi-tibyan:34-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حَاصِبًا إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ نَجَّيْنَاهُمْ بِسَحَرٍ (٣٤) نِعْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنَا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي مَنْ شَكَرَ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ) is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also said that it is a joined (muttaṣil) one, because the storm of stones was sent upon all of them, and they perished except the family of Lot. On the first view, the storm of stones was not sent upon the family of Lot. And (سَحَرٍ) is fully declinable (munṣarif), because it is indefinite. And (نِعْمَةً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ): the majority read it in the accusative, governed by an omitted verb which the one mentioned explains. And (بِقَدَرٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, or from كُلّ, i.e. "measured out".
It is also read in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «خَلَقْنَاهُ» as a naʿt (adjective) of كُلّ or of شَيْء, and «بِقَدَرٍ» as its khabar (predicate). The accusative is stronger only because it indicates the universality of creation, whereas the nominative does not indicate its universality; rather it conveys that every created thing is by measure.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حِكْمَةٌ بَالِغَةٌ فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حِكْمَةٌ) is a badal (substitute) for «مَا», which is the fāʿil (agent) of (جَاءَهُمْ).
It may also be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).
(فَمَا تُغْنِي): (مَا) may be negating, or an interrogative in the position of the accusative by تُغْنِي. And (النُّذُرُ) is the plural of نَذِير.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ فِي الزُّبُرِ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَعَلُوهُ) is a naʿt (adjective) of شَيْء or of كُلّ, and «فِي الزُّبُرِ» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:54-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ (٥٤) فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَهَرٍ): it is read with fatḥa on the nūn, and it is a singular with a plural meaning.
It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn and the hāʾ (نُهُرٍ), as a plural, like سَقْفٌ and سُقُفٌ; and some give the hāʾ sukūn (نُهْرٍ), so it is like أَسَدٌ and أُسُدٌ. And (فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ) is a badal (substitute) for His saying «فِي جَنَّاتٍ». And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ يَدْعُو الدَّاعِ إِلَى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نُكُرٍ): with ḍamma on the nūn and the kāf, and with sukūn on the kāf; it is an adjective (ṣifa) meaning "abhorred" (مُنْكَر).
It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn, kasra on the kāf and fatḥa on the rāʾ (نُكِرَ), as a passive verb.

ukberi-tibyan:7-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ (٧) مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ يَقُولُ الْكَافِرُونَ هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خُشَّعًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and regarding what governs it there are two views.
First: يَدْعُو, i.e. "the caller calls them", the owner of the ḥāl being the omitted pronoun. And «أَبْصَارُهُمْ» is nominative by خُشَّعًا; the plural may govern because it is a broken plural. Second: what governs it is «يَخْرُجُونَ».
It has also been read خَاشِعًا, the implied wording being "a group humbled"; it was not made feminine because the femininity of the agent is the femininity of a plural, which is not real (femininity). خَاشِعًا may also be accusative by يَدْعُو as its object.
On this view «يَخْرُجُونَ» is a ḥāl from the owners of the eyes.
And (كَأَنَّهُمْ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَخْرُجُونَ».
And (مُهْطِعِينَ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُنْتَشِرٌ» according to some; this is far-fetched, because the pronoun in «مُنْتَشِرٌ» is for the locusts; rather it is a ḥāl from (the subject of) «يَخْرُجُونَ», or from the omitted pronoun.
And (يَقُولُ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُهْطِعِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ فَكَذَّبُوا عَبْدَنَا وَقَالُوا مَجْنُونٌ وَازْدُجِرَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَازْدُجِرَ): the dāl is a substitute for the tāʾ, because the tāʾ is voiceless (mahmūsa) and the zāy is voiced (majhūra), so it was replaced by a voiced letter sharing its point of articulation, namely the dāl.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qamar
Meccan
﷽
﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾: the exegetes are agreed — and we have narrated it from trustworthy people of knowledge — that the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Isḥāq «[Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj himself.]» said: A group who have strayed from the right course and from what the people of knowledge hold claimed that its interpretation is that the moon will split on the Day of Resurrection. But the matter is clear from the wording and from the consensus of the people of knowledge, because of His saying: ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2] — so how could this be at the Resurrection?
Abū Isḥāq said — and all that is dictated to you on this is what Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to me — he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas: «that the people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, so he showed them the moon twice — its splitting», and he used to mention this ḥadīth at this verse: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Qatāda, from Anas, who said: "The moon split into two parts."
Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Ḥirmī ibn ʿUmāra narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪd «[Translator's note: so in the source; possibly a misprint for Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd.]» narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Anas, who said: «"The people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, and the moon split in Mecca twice, and He said: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]"», meaning: passing away. Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr narrated to us, he said: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The moon split, and I saw the mountain between the two gaps of the moon." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh — concerning His saying ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — he said: "The moon split until I saw the mountain between the two halves of the moon." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: «"The moon split while we were with the Prophet ﷺ at Minā, until one part of it went behind the mountain, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba and Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, and from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from Abū Masʿūd, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Prophet ﷺ into two parts, one part above the mountain and one part below it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Masʿūd «[Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel chains have Musaddad.]» narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿUmar, the like of it. Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two pieces, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'Bear witness, bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī said — and he narrated it to us another time — from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «"The moon split into two pieces, so that we saw it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr narrated to us, from Sulaymān — meaning Ibn Kathīr — from Ḥuṣayn, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts, on this mountain and on this mountain, and the people said: 'Muḥammad has bewitched us.' A man said: 'If he has bewitched you, he has not bewitched all the people.'"» And Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Three things that Allah has mentioned in the Qurʾān have already come to pass: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two pieces, so that the people saw it." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās — concerning His saying ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — he said: "It happened before the Hijra: the moon split, so that they saw its two pieces." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr said, from ʿIkrima, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the idolaters said: 'The moon has been bewitched, the moon has been bewitched!' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrima: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the idolaters said: 'The moon has been bewitched, the moon has been bewitched!' So there came down: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿĀrim ibn al-Faḍl and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib «[Translator's note: so in the source; the name ʿIkrima in this chain looks out of place.]», from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who said: "I set out with my father on Friday, and Ḥudhayfa addressed us — and Sulaymān said in his narration: Ḥudhayfa gave the sermon while he was at al-Madāʾin — and he recited ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾, then said: 'Indeed, the Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race.'" Sulaymān said in his narration: "So I said to my father: 'O father, will the horses be set loose tomorrow?!'" And ʿĀrim said in his narration: "So I said to my father: 'Will the people race tomorrow?!' When the following Friday came, he addressed us and recited ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ and said: 'Indeed, the Hour has drawn near, and the moon split in the time of your Prophet ﷺ. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race; the goal is the Fire, and the winner is the one who races to Paradise.'" Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabīb, who said: "We were at al-Madāʾin and came to the Friday prayer, and Ḥudhayfa addressed us. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'To proceed: Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race; indeed, the goal is the Fire.' When the next Friday came, he addressed us; he praised Allah and extolled Him" — he said — "and said the like of what he had said, and said: 'The winner is the one who races to Paradise.'" Ismāʿīl narrated to us: ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sulaymān and Qaṭar «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Fiṭr.]», from Muslim, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The inescapable punishment (al-lizām) has passed, the great seizure (al-baṭsha) has passed, the smoke (al-dukhān) has passed, and al-Rūm (the Romans) has passed." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Ibn Zayd said: "The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and half of it was seen on Quʿayqiʿān and the other half on Abū Qays «[Translator's note: i.e. Mount Abū Qubays, so written in the source.]»."

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فانْتَصِرْ﴾: the reading is ﴿أنِّي﴾ with fatḥa on the alif, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar the grammarian read "إنِّي" with kasra on the alif. Sībawayh explained "إنِّي" with kasra, saying: it is on the intention of "saying" (qawl), in the sense of: "So he called upon his Lord and said: 'I am overcome.'" He said: and similar to it is ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]; the meaning is: "They said: 'We only worship them so that they may bring us near.'" And whoever reads with fatḥa — and that is the proper way — the meaning is: "He called upon his Lord with [the words] that I am overcome."

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾: the meaning is: "So We answered his supplication and helped him." And He made clear the help with which he was helped, saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾: pouring down violently.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿وَفَجَّرْنا الأرْضَ عُيُونًا﴾: this is the majority reading, ﴿عُيُونًا﴾ with ḍamma; it has also been transmitted as "عِيُونًا", with kasra on the ʿayn, and that is poor in Arabic.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فالتَقى الماءُ عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾: meaning the water of the sky and of the earth. He did not say "fa-ltaqā l-māʾāni" (the two waters met), though had it been so it would have been permissible; but "الماءُ" is a noun that comprises the water of the earth and the water of the sky. The meaning of ﴿عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ is: which had been decreed in the Preserved Tablet. And it has been said: "قَدْ قُدِرَ" means the amount of the sky's water was like the amount of the earth's water.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَحَمَلْناهُ عَلى ذاتِ ألْواحٍ ودُسُرٍ﴾: the meaning is: "on a ship made of planks". "اَلدُّسُرُ" is the name for the nails and the cords with which the planks are bound. Everything like nailing, or driving one thing into another with force and great compulsion, is "دَسْرٌ"; one says "dasartu l-mismāra, adsuruhu, wa-adsiruhu" (I drove in the nail). "اَلدُّسُرُ": its singular is "دِسارٌ", like "حِمارٌ" and "حُمُرٌ".

zajjaj:14-14.t:
And His saying: ﴿لِمَن كانَ كُفِرَ﴾, that is: We did that as a recompense for Nūḥ and his companions, that is: We saved him and those who believed with him, and drowned those who denied him, as a recompense for what was done to him.
And His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأعْيُنِنا﴾, that is: it sails within Our sight and under Our protection.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْناها آيَةً﴾, that is: We left this deed and the matter of Nūḥ's ship as a sign, that is: a mark from which a lesson may be taken. ﴿فَهَلْ مِن مُدَّكِرٍ﴾: the reading is with the undotted dāl. Its origin is "مُذْتَكِرٌ", with dhāl and tāʾ, but the tāʾ was replaced by dāl — and the dhāl is from the place of articulation of the tāʾ, and is closer to the dāl than to the tāʾ — and then the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl. This is the proper way, I mean the reading with the undotted dāl. Some Arabs said "مُذَّكِرٍ", with the dotted dhāl, assimilating the second into the first; but this is not the proper way — the proper way is assimilating the first into the second.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾, that is: passing away; and it has been said: lasting.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكُلُّ أمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: its interpretation is that the deeds of the people of the Fire become settled for them, and the deeds of the people of Paradise become settled for them.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَهم مِنَ الأنْباءِ ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾: meaning of the reports of those who went before them and were destroyed for their denial. ﴿ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾, that is: that in which there is a restraint. You say: "nahaytuhu fa-ntahā" (I forbade him and he desisted) and "zajartuhu fa-zdajara" (I rebuked him and he refrained). The origin is "fa-ztajara", with tāʾ, but when the tāʾ comes after a zāy it is replaced by a dāl, as in "مُزْدانٌ", whose origin is "مُزْتانٌ", and likewise "مُزْتَجَرٌ". It was replaced by a dāl only because the tāʾ is a voiceless (mahmūs) letter and the zāy a voiced (majhūr) letter, so in place of the tāʾ there was substituted a voiced letter, namely dāl. This is understood only by one who has mastered the whole of Arabic, and it is at the end of the Book of Sībawayh. What should be said to the learner is: when you form "اِفْتَعَلَ" or "مُفْتَعَلٌ" from a root whose first letter is zāy, change the tāʾ into a dāl, as in "اِزْدَجَرَ" and "مُزْدَجَرٌ".

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ بالِغَةٌ﴾: "حِكْمَةٌ" is nominative as a badal (substitute) for "ما"; the meaning is: "And there has come to them far-reaching wisdom." And if you wish, you may make "حِكْمَةٌ" nominative with "هُوَ" implied; the meaning is: "It is far-reaching wisdom."
And His saying: ﴿فَما تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾: "ما" may be interrogative in form with the meaning of rebuke, so that the meaning is: "So what do the warnings avail?!", and its position would be accusative by "تُغْنِ". And it may be a negation, in the sense of: "So the warnings do not avail."

zajjaj:6-6.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهم يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾: the complete pause (waqf al-tamām) is at ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
And His saying ﴿إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾: to what they used to deny of the resurrection. "So turn away from them; on the day [such-and-such happens]" as in the verse «[Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]». "يَوْمَ" is accusative by His saying ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]. As for the omission of the wāw from "يَدْعُ" in the written text, it is because it is dropped in pronunciation owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the wāw of "يَدْعُو" and the lām of "اَلدّاعِ"; so it was written as it is pronounced. As for "اَلدّاعِ", retaining the yāʾ in it is better, though omitting it is permissible, because the kasra indicates it.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهُمْ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "They come out of the graves, their eyes humbled." It has also been read "خاشِعًا أبْصارُهُمْ", and Ibn Masʿūd read "خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ". With active participles, when they precede a plural, you may use the singular, as in "خاشِعًا أبْصارُهُمْ"; you may use the singular with the feminine, because of the femininity of the group: "خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ"; and you may use the plural, as in "خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهُمْ". You say: "marartu bi-shubbānin ḥasanin awjuhuhum" (I passed by young men handsome of face), "ḥisānin awjuhuhum" and "ḥasanatin awjuhuhum". The poet said:
؎وَشَبابٍ حَسَنٍ أوْجُهُهم ∗∗∗ مِن إيادِ بْنِ نِزارِ بْنِ مَعَدِ
(And young men handsome of face, of Iyād son of Nizār son of Maʿadd.)

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ إلى الدّاعِ﴾ is also accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "They come out, their eyes humbled, مُهْطِعِينَ." The meaning of ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ is: staring, not lifting their eyes away.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
And His saying: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهم قَوْمُ نُوحٍ﴾, that is: the people of Nūḥ denied Nūḥ before your people, O Muḥammad.
﴿وَقالُوا مَجْنُونٌ وازْدُجِرَ﴾: and they said "He is mad", just as your people said of you, O Muḥammad ﷺ, and upon them all.
"وازْدُجِرَ": he was rebuked with abuse. We have already explained what there is in "مُزْدَجَرٌ" concerning the change of the tāʾ into a dāl; the origin of this is "وازْتُجِرَ".

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنا القُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ﴾: the meaning is "We have made it easy". And it has been said: the books of the followers of other religions — such as the Torah and the Gospel — are recited by their followers only by looking at the text, and they hardly memorise their books from beginning to end as the Qurʾān is memorised.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا﴾: "صَرْصَرًا" means intensely cold.
﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾: meaning "نَحْسٍ" (ill-omened), and "مُسْتَمِرٍّ" means lasting in its ill omen. And it has been said: on a Wednesday at the end of the month that does not come round again.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنْـزِعُ النّاسَ كَأنَّهم أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾: "كَأنَّهُمْ" here is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "It plucks the people out, resembling uprooted palm trees." Al-munqaʿir is that which is cut off from its roots; the wind would throw them down on their faces.
And His saying: ﴿مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾: "النَّخْلُ" (palm trees) is treated as masculine and feminine; one says "hādhā nakhlun" and "hādhihi nakhlun". So "مُنْقَعِرٌ" follows those who say "hādhā nakhlun"; and for those who say "hādhihi nakhlun", it is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 7].

zajjaj:23-23.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾: "اَلنُّذُرُ" is the plural of "نَذِيرٌ" (warner).

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿فَقالُوا أبَشَرًا مِنّا واحِدًا نَتَّبِعُهُ﴾: "بَشَرًا" is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "Shall we follow a human being?!"
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا إذًا لَفي ضَلالٍ وسُعُرٍ﴾: its meaning is: "Then we would indeed be in error and madness." One says "nāqatun masʿūra" (a crazed she-camel) when she has madness. And it may be in the sense of: "If we follow him, we are in error and in torment."

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿بَلْ هو كَذّابٌ أشِرٌ﴾: "أشِرٌ" is in the sense of "بَطِرٌ" (insolent, arrogant). One says "ashira, yaʾsharu, asharan, fa-huwa ashirun", like "baṭira, yabṭaru, baṭaran, fa-huwa baṭirun".

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا مُرْسِلُو النّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ﴾: "فِتْنَةً" is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "We are sending the she-camel in order to try them", that is: to test them.

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهم أنَّ الماءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهم كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾, that is: the water is divided between the she-camel and Thamūd: she has a day and they have a day. And this is its meaning: "Every drinking turn is attended: the people attend the drinking one day, and the she-camel attends one day."

zajjaj:29-29.t:
﴿فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهم فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾: he used to be called "Aḥmar Thamūd" (the Red One of Thamūd) and "Uḥaymir Thamūd" (the little Red One of Thamūd). The Arabs err and make him "Aḥmar ʿĀd", and use him as a proverb for ill omen. Zuhayr said, describing a war:
؎فَتُنْتِجْ لَكم غِلْمانَ أشْأمُ كُلُّهم ∗∗∗ كَأحْمَرِ عادٍ ثُمَّ تُرْضِعْ فَتَفْطِمِ
(It will bear for you sons of ill omen, all of them like the Red One of ʿĀd; then it will suckle and wean.)
And the meaning of ﴿فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾ is: he undertook the hamstringing of the she-camel, and he hamstrung her, and so attained what he wanted.

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ المُحْتَظِرِ﴾, with kasra on the ẓāʾ; and it is also read "اَلْمُحْتَظَرِ", with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ. "اَلْهَشِيمُ" is leaves that have dried up, broken and crumbled; that is: they became like the dry stubble which the owner of the enclosure (al-ḥaẓīra) gathers, that is: it had reached the utmost dryness, to the point of being gathered to be burned. Whoever reads "اَلْمُحْتَظَرِ" with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, it is a noun for the enclosure; the meaning is: "like the stubble of the place in which stubble is enclosed". And whoever reads ﴿المُحْتَظِرِ﴾ with kasra on the ẓāʾ, it is a reference to the one who gathers the stubble of firewood in the enclosure, for he is "اَلْمُحْتَظِرُ", because he is the agent.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إلا آلَ لُوطٍ نَجَّيْناهم بِسَحَرٍ﴾: "سَحَرٍ", when it is indefinite, meaning some pre-dawn time or other, is declinable (fully inflected, munṣarif). You say: "ataytu Zaydan saḥaran mina l-asḥār" (I came to Zayd at a pre-dawn time). But if you mean the pre-dawn of your current day, you say: "ataytuhu li-saḥarin yā hādhā" «[Translator's note: so in the source, with nunation; given the point being made, the intended form is presumably diptote, li-saḥara.]» and "ataytuhu saḥara yā hādhā" (I came to him this pre-dawn, you there).

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿نِعْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا﴾ is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "We saved them in order to bestow favour upon them." Had it been read "نِعْمَةٌ مِن عِنْدِنا" (nominative), it would be a valid way, and the meaning would be: "That is a favour from Us; Our saving them is a favour from Us." Abū Isḥāq said: But I know of no one who read it so, so do not read it so unless a sound transmission is established. Our teachers among the people of knowledge said: Reading (qirāʾa) is a followed practice (sunna muttabaʿa), and they do not hold that anyone may read according to what is permissible in Arabic if no sound transmission is established.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنا أعْيُنَهُمْ﴾: the people of Lūṭ tried to seduce Lūṭ away from his guests, who were the angels. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded Jibrīl, and he struck their eyes with his wings with a single stroke, took them away and effaced them, and they remained in the house blind and bewildered.

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهم بُكْرَةً عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: "بُكُرَةً" and "غُدْوَةً" (early morning), when they are indefinite, take nunation and are declinable; but when you mean by them the early morning of your current day, you do not make them declinable. So "بُكْرَةً" here is indefinite. Had it been read "بُكُرَةَ عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ" and "نَجَّيْناهم بِسَحَرَ نِعْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا", both would have been permissible in Arabic, the meaning being "the early morning of their day" and "the pre-dawn of their day". But the indefinite, declinable form is better in this verse, and no transmission has been established that it was on such-and-such a day of such-and-such a month.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أكُفّارُكم خَيْرٌ مِن أُولَئِكُمْ﴾, that is: are your disbelievers, O company of Arabs and those to whom the Prophet ﷺ was sent, better than those — that is, the disbelievers whose stories and destruction We have mentioned? ﴿أمْ لَكم بَراءَةٌ في الزُّبُرِ﴾, that is: or has it come to you in the scriptures that you are absolved of what would necessitate your ʿidāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source (عداءكم, "enmity towards you"); possibly a misprint for عذابكم, "your punishment".]»?

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾: the meaning is: "Rather, do they say: 'We are a united host, victorious', and so presume upon strength and unity against you?!"
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He would destroy them from the very direction from which they reckoned on victory, and said: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would make him prevail over them and make His word the highest, saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]; and this defeat was on the day of Badr.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾: the meaning is "and they will turn their backs (al-adbār, plural)", as He said: ﴿وَإنْ يُقاتِلُوكم يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 111]. Likewise is the meaning in His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في جَنّاتٍ ونَهَرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 54]; the meaning is "in gardens and rivers". The singular noun indicates the plural, and is made to suffice for the plural. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl recited:
؎بِها جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فَأمّا عِظامُها ∗∗∗ فَبِيضٌ وأمّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيبُ
(In it are the carcasses of exhausted camels: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skin, it is hard.)
They mean "and as for their skins (julūduhā)". And he recited:
؎فِي حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقَدْ شُجِينا
(In your throat is a bone, and we have choked.)
The meaning is: in your throats are bones. And as he said:
؎كُلُوا في بَعْضِ بَطْنِكم تَعِفُّوا ∗∗∗ فَإنَّ زَمانَكم زَمَنٌ خَمِيصٌ
(Eat with part of your belly and stay restrained, for your time is a time of hunger.)
The meaning is: "Eat with part of your bellies."

zajjaj:46-46.t: Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾, that is: the killing and captivity that befell them on the day of Badr do not lighten for them anything of the punishment of the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾, that is: more severe. Every dāhiya (calamity) means the severe matter for which no remedy can be found. And the meaning of ﴿وَأمَرُّ﴾ is: more bitter than killing and captivity.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُجْرِمِينَ في ضَلالٍ وسُعُرٍ﴾: it is in the exegesis that this verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.

zajjaj:48-48.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ في النّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾: the meaning is: "It will be said to them: Taste the touch of Saqar."

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿إنّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾, that is: everything We have created is decreed and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs. "كُلَّ شَيْءٍ" is accusative by an implied verb; the meaning is: "We have created everything; We created it by measure." This is indicated by ﴿وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ في الزُّبُرِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 52] ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وكَبِيرٍ مُسْتَطَرٌ﴾ [al-Qamar: 53]. "مُسْتَطَرٌ" is a passive participle from "اَلسَّطْرُ" (writing in lines); the meaning is: "Every sin, small and great, is recorded — written against those who do it before they do it, and written for them and against them when they do it, so that they may be recompensed for their deeds."
